Surah al-Jathiyah

Thirty-seven verses, Meccan

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

﴿Ha, Mim.﴾ ﴿The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the All-Mighty, the All-Wise.﴾ ﴿Indeed, in the heavens and the earth are signs for the believers.﴾ ﴿And in your creation and what He disperses of creatures are signs for a people who are certain.﴾ ﴿And in the alternation of the night and the day and what Allah has sent down from the sky of provision and given life thereby to the earth after its death, and the changing of the winds, are signs for a people who reason.﴾ ﴿These are the verses of Allah which We recite to you in truth. So in what statement after Allah and His verses will they believe?﴾

And in it are issues:

The first issue: Know that in His saying ﴿Ha, Mim﴾ ﴿The revelation of the Book﴾ there are several aspects:

The first: that ﴿Ha, Mim﴾ is a subject (mubtada') and ﴿The revelation of the Book﴾ is its predicate (khabar). On this assumption, an elided genitive (mudaf) must be supplied, and the sense is: "The revelation of Ha, Mim is the revelation of the Book." And ﴿from Allah﴾ is a complement (silah) of "revelation."

The second: that His saying ﴿Ha, Mim﴾ is in the sense of "this is Ha, Mim," and then we say: ﴿The revelation of the Book﴾ proceeds from Allah, the All-Mighty, the All-Wise.

The third: that ﴿Ha, Mim﴾ is an oath, and ﴿The revelation of the Book﴾ is its qualifier (na't), and the answer to the oath is ﴿Indeed, in the heavens…﴾. The sense is: "By Ha, Mim, which is the revelation of the Book, the matter is such and such."

The second issue: His saying ﴿the All-Mighty, the All-Wise﴾ may be taken as qualifiers of "the Book," and it may be taken as qualifiers of Allah, the Exalted. However, the latter is preferable, and this is indicated by several aspects:

The first: if we make them qualifiers of Allah, the Exalted, that is a literal (haqiqah) usage; if we make them qualifiers of "the Book," that is a figurative (majaz) usage, and the literal is preferable to the figurative.

The second: that closeness of reference brings preponderance (al-rujhan)

Page 221

The third: if we take "the All-Mighty, the All-Wise" as qualifiers of Allah, that is a pointer to the proof that the Qur'an is true, because His being All-Mighty indicates that He is capable of all possibilities (al-mumkinat), and His being All-Wise indicates that He is knowing of all knowables and free of all needs. From the combination of His being "All-Mighty, All-Wise" we obtain that He is capable of all possibilities, knowing of all knowables, and free of all needs, and whatever is such, folly and falsehood cannot proceed from it. And when this is so, the manifestation of a miracle is a proof of truthfulness. Thus it is established that if we take His being All-Mighty and All-Wise as two attributes of Allah, the Exalted, this benefit results; but if we take them as two attributes of the Book, this benefit does not result. So the former is preferable, and Allah knows best.

* * *

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, in the heavens and the earth are signs for the believers﴾, and in it are discussions:

The first discussion: His saying ﴿Indeed, in the heavens and the earth are signs﴾ may be taken according to its apparent meaning, because in the very essences of the heavens and the earth there occur states that indicate the existence of Allah, the Exalted, such as their measures, their modes, and their motions. Also, the sun, the moon, the stars, the mountains, and the seas exist in the heavens and the earth and are signs. It is also possible that the meaning is "Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth," as stated in Surah al-Baqarah in His saying: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth﴾ [al-Baqarah: 164], and this indicates the existence of the capable, choosing Agent, in explanation of His saying: ﴿Praise be to Allah who created the heavens and the earth﴾ [al-An'am: 1].

The second discussion: We have mentioned the many aspects of the heavens and the earth indicating the existence of the capable, choosing God in the explanation of His saying ﴿Praise be to Allah who created the heavens and the earth﴾, and there is no harm in repeating some of them. So we say: they indicate the existence of God in several aspects:

The first: they are bodies that do not escape accidents (hawadith), and what does not escape accidents is originated (hadith). Therefore these bodies are originated, and every originated thing has an originator.

The second: they are composed of parts, and those parts are alike, since we have shown that bodies are alike. And some of those parts occur in depth but not on the surface, and some on the surface but not in depth. So the occurrence of each part in the place where it occurs is among the permissibles (jA'izat), and every permissible must have a determiner and a specifier.

The third: the spheres (aflak) and the elements (al-'anasir), although alike in the complete corporeal quiddity, each one is specified by a determined attribute, such as heat, cold, subtlety, and celestial and elemental density. So this is a permissible matter, and it must have a determiner.

The fourth: the bodies of the stars differ in colors, such as the dullness of Saturn, the whiteness of Jupiter, the redness of Mars, the dazzling light of the sun, the brightness of Venus, the yellowness of Mercury, and the dimness of the moon. Also, some of them are fortunate and some unlucky, some are diurnal and masculine, and some nocturnal and feminine. And we have shown that bodies in their essences are alike, so the difference of attributes must be because the capable, choosing God specified each of them with its determined attribute.

The fifth: every sphere is specified with motion in a particular direction and with a single measure of speed and slowness, and all of this is likewise among the permissibles, so a choosing Agent is necessary.

The sixth: every sphere is specified with something determined, and all of this is likewise among the permissibles, so a choosing Agent is necessary. The complete aspects are mentioned in the explanation of those verses.

The third discussion: His saying ﴿signs for the believers﴾ requires that these signs be specific to the believers. The Mu'tazilah said: they are signs for the believer and the unbeliever, but since the believer benefits from them and not the unbeliever, their being signs is attributed to the believers. An analogue is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿a guidance for the God-fearing﴾ [al-Baqarah: 2], for it is a guidance for all people, as He said: ﴿a guidance for mankind﴾ [al-Baqarah: 185], but since the believer alone benefits from it, it was said: ﴿a guidance for the God-fearing.﴾ So likewise here. The Companions (al-Ash'ariyyah) said: the proof and the sign is that upon whose knowledge the attainment of knowledge is consequent, and that knowledge is produced only by the creation of Allah, the Exalted, not by the proof's necessitating it. Allah, the Exalted, created that knowledge only for the believer, not for the unbeliever, so it is a sign and a proof with respect to the believer, not with respect to the unbeliever. And Allah knows best.

* * *

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And in your creation and what He disperses of creatures are signs for a people who are certain﴾, and in it are discussions:

The first discussion: The author of al-Kashshaf said: His saying ﴿and what He disperses﴾ is conjoined to "creation," which is governed by the attached pronoun, not to the pronoun of possession itself, since the genitive is an attached pronoun in the genitive case, and conjoining upon it is considered ugly. So one does not say "I passed by you and Zayd." For this reason they criticized the reading of Hamzah: "by whom you ask one another, and the wombs" in the genitive, with "and the wombs" in the genitive. Likewise, those who found this conjunction ugly do not say "I passed by you, you and Zayd."

The second discussion: Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read (āyātin) with a kasrah on the tā', and likewise the one after it, "and the changing of the winds, signs," while the rest read both with a raf'. As for the raf', it is on two grounds mentioned by al-Mubarrad, al-Zajjaj, and Abu 'Ali:

One of them: conjunction upon the place (mahall) of "inna" and what it governs, since their place is nominative by inception, so the raf' is taken as applying to the place, as you say: "Inna Zaydan muntalliqun wa 'Amr," and "Anna Allaha bari'un mina al-mushrikina wa rasuluhu" [al-Tawbah: 3], because the sense of His saying "Anna Allaha bari'" is that one would say: "Allah is free of the polytheists, and His Messenger."

The second ground: that His saying ﴿and in your creation﴾ is resumptive (musta'nafan), and the speech is a sentence conjoined to another sentence, as you say: "Inna Zaydan muntalaqun wa 'Amr kateb," where you make your saying "wa 'Amr kateb" another statement, as you say: "Zayd is in the house, and I go out tomorrow to such-and-such a town," where you have related two reports and joined one to the other with "wa." This ground is the preference of Abu al-Hasan and al-Farra'.

As for the ground of the reading with the accusative, it is conjunction upon His saying ﴿Indeed, in the heavens﴾, in the sense of "and indeed, in your creation are signs." They say this reading is in the reading of Ubayy and 'Abd Allah ("la-āyātin"), and the entry of the lam indicates that the speech is governed by "inna."

The third discussion: His saying ﴿and in your creation﴾ means the creation of man, and His saying ﴿and what He disperses of creatures﴾ points to the creation of the rest of the animals. The aspect of its indicating the existence of the capable, choosing God is that bodies are equal, so the specification of each of the members with being the determined one, its determined attribute, and its determined shape must be by the specification of the capable, choosing one. Included in this category is its passage from one age to another age and from one state to another state. The thorough treatment of this topic has already preceded.

* * *

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿the alternation of the night and the day﴾, and this alternation occurs in several aspects:

First: the replacement of the day by the night and the reverse of that.

Second: that sometimes the length of the day exceeds the length of the night and sometimes the reverse, and in proportion to what the day increases in summer, the night increases in winter.

Third: the variation of the risings of the sun in the days of the year.

* * *

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿and what Allah has sent down from the sky of provision, and given life thereby to the earth after its death﴾, and this indicates the doctrine of the choosing Agent in several aspects:

First: the production of the clouds and the sending down of rain from them.

Second: the生 growth of plants from that seed fallen into the earth.

Third: the generation of the various kinds, which are the stalk of the tree, its branches, its leaves and its fruits, and then of those fruits, some in which the skin encloses the kernel, like the walnut and almond; some in which the kernel encloses the skin, like the apricot and peach; and some which are free of skin, like the fig. So the generation of the divisions of plants, with the multitude of their kinds and the diversity of their divisions, indicates the soundness of the doctrine of the choosing, wise, merciful Agent.

Then He said: ﴿and the changing of the winds﴾, and they divide into many divisions according to various classifications: among them are the eastern and western, the northern and southern; among them are the hot and the cold; among them are the beneficial winds and the harmful winds. And when Allah, the Exalted, mentioned these many kinds of proofs, He said that they are ﴿signs for a people who reason.﴾

Know that Allah, the Exalted, gathered these proofs in Surah al-Baqarah, saying: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the alternation of the night and the day, and the ship that runs in the sea with what benefits mankind, and what Allah sends down from the sky of water and gives life thereby to the earth after its death, and disperses therein every kind of creature, and the changing of the winds and the clouds subjected between the sky and the earth are signs for a people who reason﴾ [al-Baqarah: 164]. So Allah, the Exalted, mentioned these eight divisions of proofs, and the difference between the two passages is in several aspects:

The first: that He, the Exalted, said in Surah al-Baqarah, "Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth," and said here, "Indeed, in the heavens"; and the sound opinion of our companions is that creation is the very thing created. He mentioned the word "creation" in Surah al-Baqarah and did not mention it in this surah, as an indication that there is no difference between saying "the heavens" and saying "the creation of the heavens," and this is evidence that creation is the very thing created.

The second: that there He mentioned eight kinds of proofs, and here He mentioned six kinds, omitting from them the ship and the clouds; the reason being that the axis of the motion of the ship and the clouds is upon the varying winds, so the mention of the winds, which is like a cause, dispenses with mentioning those two.

The third difference: he gathered them all and mentioned for them one single pause (maqta'), whereas here he arranged them into three pauses. The purpose is to alert that each one of them requires being considered separately with a complete and healing contemplation.

The fourth: in this place, He, may He be exalted, mentioned three pauses: the first is "yu'minun" (they believe), the second is "yuqinun" (they are certain), and the third is "ya'qilun" (they reason). I think the reason for this order is that it was said: "If you are among the believers, then understand these proofs. If you are not among the believers, but rather among the seekers of truth and certainty, then understand these proofs. And if you are neither among the believers nor among the certain, then at least you should be among the group of the rational; so strive to know these proofs."

Know that many of the jurists (fuqaha') say that the Qur'an does not contain the sciences that the theologians (mutakallimun) investigate; rather, it contains nothing but what relates to the rulings (ahkam) and jurisprudence (fiqh). This is a tremendous heedlessness, because there is no long surah in the Qur'an devoted solely to mentioning the rulings, while there are many surahs in it, especially the Meccan ones, which contain nothing but the mention of the proofs of tawhid (monotheism), prophethood, resurrection and the Last Day. All of this belongs to the sciences of the usuliyyun (scholars of the foundations of belief). Whoever reflects will know that the scholars of usul (uṣūl al-fiqh and uṣūl al-dīn) possess nothing but the detailed explanation of what the Qur'an contains in summary form.
* * *
Then He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿This is the signs of Allah, which We recite to you in truth﴾. What is meant by His words ﴿in truth﴾ is that their soundness is known through rational proofs. This is because knowledge that they are true and sound is either derived from transmission (naql) or from reason ('aql). The first is invalid, because the soundness of transmitted proofs depends on prior knowledge of the establishment of a God who is Knowing, Powerful and Wise, and of the establishment of prophethood, and of how miracles indicate its truth. So if we proved these foundations by transmitted proofs, circularity (dawr) would follow, and that is invalid. Since this has been shown to be invalid, it is established that knowledge of the reality of these proofs cannot be acquired except by pure reason. And since this is so, His words ﴿This is the signs of Allah, which We recite to you in truth﴾ are among the greatest evidences for encouraging the study of the foundations of belief ('ilm al-usul) and the establishment of rational investigations.
* * *
Then He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Then in what statement after Allah and His signs will they believe?﴾ He means that whoever is not benefited by these signs, then there is nothing after them that could benefit him. By this he refuted the view of those who claim that imitation (taqlid) is sufficient, and he made clear that it is obligatory for the responsible person (mukallaf) to reflect upon the proofs of the religion of Allah. His words ﴿yu'minun﴾ were read with the ya' and with the ta'; Abu 'Ubayda preferred the ya' because before it there is a third-person reference, namely His words ﴿for a people who are certain﴾ and ﴿for a people who reason﴾. If it is said: at the beginning of the speech there is an address in the second person, namely His words ﴿and in your creation﴾, we say: the third-person reference we mentioned is closer to the disputed letter, and the closer is more appropriate. The reasoning of the one who read it in the second person is that "qul" (say) is implied in it, meaning: say to them, "Then in what statement after this will you believe?"

The Mu'tazilah said: they are signs for the believer and the unbeliever, but since the believer benefits from them and not the unbeliever, their being signs is attributed to the believers. An analogue is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿a guidance for the God-fearing﴾ [al-Baqarah: 2], for it is a guidance for all people, as He said: ﴿a guidance for mankind﴾ [al-Baqarah: 185], but since the believer alone benefits from it, it was said: ﴿a guidance for the God-fearing.﴾ So likewise here. The Companions (al-Ash'ariyyah) said: the proof and the sign is that upon whose knowledge the attainment of knowledge is consequent, and that knowledge is produced only by the creation of Allah, the Exalted, not by the proof's necessitating it. Allah, the Exalted, created that knowledge only for the believer, not for the unbeliever, so it is a sign and a proof with respect to the believer, not with respect to the unbeliever. And Allah knows best.

* * *

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And in your creation and what He disperses of creatures are signs for a people who are certain﴾, and in it are discussions:

The first discussion: The author of al-Kashshaf said: His saying ﴿and what He disperses﴾ is conjoined to "creation," which is governed by the attached pronoun, not to the pronoun of possession itself, since the genitive is an attached pronoun in the genitive case, and conjoining upon it is considered ugly. So one does not say "I passed by you and Zayd." For this reason they criticized the reading of Hamzah: "by whom you ask one another, and the wombs" in the genitive, with "and the wombs" in the genitive. Likewise, those who found this conjunction ugly do not say "I passed by you, you and Zayd."

The second discussion: Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read (āyātin) with a kasrah on the tā', and likewise the one after it, "and the changing of the winds, signs," while the rest read both with a raf'. As for the raf', it is on two grounds mentioned by al-Mubarrad, al-Zajjaj, and Abu 'Ali:

One of them: conjunction upon the place (mahall) of "inna" and what it governs, since their place is nominative by inception, so the raf' is taken as applying to the place, as you say: "Inna Zaydan muntalliqun wa 'Amr," and "Anna Allaha bari'un mina al-mushrikina wa rasuluhu" [al-Tawbah: 3], because the sense of His saying "Anna Allaha bari'" is that one would say: "Allah is free of the polytheists, and His Messenger."

The second ground: that His saying ﴿and in your creation﴾ is resumptive (musta'nafan), and the speech is a sentence conjoined to another sentence, as you say: "Inna Zaydan muntalaqun wa 'Amr kateb," where you make your saying "wa 'Amr kateb" another statement, as you say: "Zayd is in the house, and I go out tomorrow to such-and-such a town," where you have related two reports and joined one to the other with "wa." This ground is the preference of Abu al-Hasan and al-Farra'.

As for the ground of the reading with the accusative, it is conjunction upon His saying ﴿Indeed, in the heavens﴾, in the sense of "and indeed, in your creation are signs." They say this reading is in the reading of Ubayy and 'Abd Allah ("la-āyātin"), and the entry of the lam indicates that the speech is governed by "inna."

The third discussion: His saying ﴿and in your creation﴾ means the creation of man, and His saying ﴿and what He disperses of creatures﴾ points to the creation of the rest of the animals. The aspect of its indicating the existence of the capable, choosing God is that bodies are equal, so the specification of each of the members with being the determined one, its determined attribute, and its determined shape must be by the specification of the capable, choosing one. Included in this category is its passage from one age to another age and from one state to another state. The thorough treatment of this topic has already preceded.

* * *

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿the alternation of the night and the day﴾, and this alternation occurs in several aspects:

First: the replacement of the day by the night and the reverse of that.

Second: that sometimes the length of the day exceeds the length of the night and sometimes the reverse, and in proportion to what the day increases in summer, the night increases in winter.

Third: the variation of the risings of the sun in the days of the year.

* * *

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿and what Allah has sent down from the sky of provision, and given life thereby to the earth after its death﴾, and this indicates the doctrine of the choosing Agent in several aspects:

First: the production of the clouds and the sending down of rain from them.

Second: the生 growth of plants from that seed fallen into the earth.

Third: the generation of the various kinds, which are the stalk of the tree, its branches, its leaves and its fruits, and then of those fruits, some in which the skin encloses the kernel, like the walnut and almond; some in which the kernel encloses the skin, like the apricot and peach; and some which are free of skin, like the fig. So the generation of the divisions of plants, with the multitude of their kinds and the diversity of their divisions, indicates the soundness of the doctrine of the choosing, wise, merciful Agent.

Page 223

Then He said: ﴿and the changing of the winds﴾, and they divide into many divisions according to various classifications: among them are the eastern and western, the northern and southern; among them are the hot and the cold; among them are the beneficial winds and the harmful winds. And when Allah, the Exalted, mentioned these many kinds of proofs, He said that they are ﴿signs for a people who reason.﴾

Know that Allah, the Exalted, gathered these proofs in Surah al-Baqarah, saying: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the alternation of the night and the day, and the ship that runs in the sea with what benefits mankind, and what Allah sends down from the sky of water and gives life thereby to the earth after its death, and disperses therein every kind of creature, and the changing of the winds and the clouds subjected between the sky and the earth are signs for a people who reason﴾ [al-Baqarah: 164]. So Allah, the Exalted, mentioned these eight divisions of proofs, and the difference between the two passages is in several aspects:

The first: that He, the Exalted, said in Surah al-Baqarah, "Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth," and said here, "Indeed, in the heavens"; and the sound opinion of our companions is that creation is the very thing created. He mentioned the word "creation" in Surah al-Baqarah and did not mention it in this surah, as an indication that there is no difference between saying "the heavens" and saying "the creation of the heavens," and this is evidence that creation is the very thing created.

The second: that there He mentioned eight kinds of proofs, and here He mentioned six kinds, omitting from them the ship and the clouds; the reason being that the axis of the motion of the ship and the clouds is upon the varying winds, so the mention of the winds, which is like a cause, dispenses with mentioning those two.

The third difference: he gathered them all and mentioned for them one single pause (maqta'), whereas here he arranged them into three pauses. The purpose is to alert that each one of them requires being considered separately with a complete and healing contemplation.

The fourth: in this place, He, may He be exalted, mentioned three pauses: the first is "yu'minun" (they believe), the second is "yuqinun" (they are certain), and the third is "ya'qilun" (they reason). I think the reason for this order is that it was said: "If you are among the believers, then understand these proofs. If you are not among the believers, but rather among the seekers of truth and certainty, then understand these proofs. And if you are neither among the believers nor among the certain, then at least you should be among the group of the rational; so strive to know these proofs."

Know that many of the jurists (fuqaha') say that the Qur'an does not contain the sciences that the theologians (mutakallimun) investigate; rather, it contains nothing but what relates to the rulings (ahkam) and jurisprudence (fiqh). This is a tremendous heedlessness, because there is no long surah in the Qur'an devoted solely to mentioning the rulings, while there are many surahs in it, especially the Meccan ones, which contain nothing but the mention of the proofs of tawhid (monotheism), prophethood, resurrection and the Last Day. All of this belongs to the sciences of the usuliyyun (scholars of the foundations of belief). Whoever reflects will know that the scholars of usul (uṣūl al-fiqh and uṣūl al-dīn) possess nothing but the detailed explanation of what the Qur'an contains in summary form.
* * *
Then He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿This is the signs of Allah, which We recite to you in truth﴾. What is meant by His words ﴿in truth﴾ is that their soundness is known through rational proofs. This is because knowledge that they are true and sound is either derived from transmission (naql) or from reason ('aql). The first is invalid, because the soundness of transmitted proofs depends on prior knowledge of the establishment of a God who is Knowing, Powerful and Wise, and of the establishment of prophethood, and of how miracles indicate its truth. So if we proved these foundations by transmitted proofs, circularity (dawr) would follow, and that is invalid. Since this has been shown to be invalid, it is established that knowledge of the reality of these proofs cannot be acquired except by pure reason. And since this is so, His words ﴿This is the signs of Allah, which We recite to you in truth﴾ are among the greatest evidences for encouraging the study of the foundations of belief ('ilm al-usul) and the establishment of rational investigations.
* * *
Then He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Then in what statement after Allah and His signs will they believe?﴾ He means that whoever is not benefited by these signs, then there is nothing after them that could benefit him. By this he refuted the view of those who claim that imitation (taqlid) is sufficient, and he made clear that it is obligatory for the responsible person (mukallaf) to reflect upon the proofs of the religion of Allah. His words ﴿yu'minun﴾ were read with the ya' and with the ta'; Abu 'Ubayda preferred the ya' because before it there is a third-person reference, namely His words ﴿for a people who are certain﴾ and ﴿for a people who reason﴾. If it is said: at the beginning of the speech there is an address in the second person, namely His words ﴿and in your creation﴾, we say: the third-person reference we mentioned is closer to the disputed letter, and the closer is more appropriate. The reasoning of the one who read it in the second person is that "qul" (say) is implied in it, meaning: say to them, "Then in what statement after this will you believe?"

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 45, verses 7–13:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Woe to every sinful liar﴾ ﴿who hears the signs of Allah recited to him, then persists arrogantly as though he had not heard them. So give him tidings of a painful punishment﴾ ﴿And when he learns anything of Our signs, he takes them in mockery. For such there is a humiliating punishment﴾ ﴿Behind them is Hell, and what they earned will not avail them at all, nor those they took as protectors besides Allah. And for them is a great punishment﴾ ﴿This is guidance, and those who disbelieve in the signs of their Lord, for them is a punishment of a painful wrath﴾.

Know that when He, exalted is He, had clarified the signs for the disbelievers, and made clear that, if they do not believe in them despite their manifestness, then by what statement after it would they believe, He followed it with a severe threat against them, saying: ﴿Woe to every sinful liar﴾. Al-Affak is the liar, and al-Athim is one who is excessive in committing sins. Know that this sinful one has two stations.

The first station: that he remains persistent in denial and arrogance. So He, exalted is He, said: ﴿who hears the signs of Allah recited to him, then persists﴾, meaning he maintains his disbelief with strength and intensity, ﴿arrogantly﴾ refusing faith in the signs, admiring what he has. It is said that it was revealed concerning al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, who used to purchase tales of the non-Arabs and occupy people with them away from listening to the Qur'an. The verse is general in every person who is characterized by the described attribute. If they say: What is the meaning of "then" (thumma) in His saying: ﴿then persists arrogantly﴾? We say: its parallel is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Praise belongs to Allah who created the heavens and the earth﴾ up to His saying: ﴿then those who disbelieve ascribe equals to their Lord﴾ [al-An'am: 1]. Its meaning is that since He, exalted is He, is the Creator of the heavens and the earth, it is far-fetched to make these idols equal to Him in worship. Likewise here, hearing the signs of Allah with their strength and manifestness, it is far-fetched that they be met with denial and aversion.

* * *
Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿as though he had not heard them﴾. The original is "ka'annahu lam yasma'ha" (as though he had not heard them), the pronoun is the pronoun of the matter (dhamir al-sha'n), and the clause's position is accusative as a circumstantial state (hal), meaning he becomes like one who did not hear.

The second station: that he moves from the station of persistence and arrogance to the station of mockery. So He said: ﴿And when he learns anything of Our signs, he takes them in mockery﴾. The proper wording of the speech would have been "ittakhadha-hu huzuwan" (he took it as mockery), meaning he took that thing as mockery. However, He, exalted is He, said "ittakhadha-ha" (he took them) to indicate that this man, whenever he perceives anything of the speech to be from among the verses that Allah, exalted is He, sent down upon Muhammad (ﷺ), he plunges into mocking all the verses, and does not limit his mockery to that single one.

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿For such there is a humiliating punishment﴾. "Ula'ika" (such) refers to ﴿every sinful liar﴾, because it encompasses all liars. Then He described the manner of that humiliating punishment, saying: ﴿Behind them is Hell﴾, meaning in front of them is Hell. The author of al-Kashshaf said: al-Wara' is a name for the direction in which a person is concealed, whether from behind or from in front. Then He clarified that what they possessed in the world does not benefit them, saying: ﴿and what they earned will not avail them at all﴾.

Then He clarified that their idols do not benefit them, saying: ﴿nor those they took as protectors besides Allah﴾, then He said: ﴿And for them is a great punishment﴾. If they say: He said before this verse: ﴿For them is a humiliating punishment﴾, so what is the benefit in His saying after it: ﴿And for them is a great punishment﴾?

We say: that the punishment being humiliating indicates that humiliation occurs along with the punishment, and that its being great indicates that it reaches the utmost extremes in being harm.

* * *
Then He said: ﴿This is guidance﴾, meaning complete in being guidance. ﴿And those who disbelieve in the signs of their Lord, for them is a punishment of a painful wrath﴾. Al-Rijz is the most severe punishment, as indicated by His saying: ﴿So We sent down upon those who wronged a wrath from the heaven﴾ [al-Baqarah: 59], and His saying: ﴿If you remove from us the wrath﴾ [al-A'raf: 134]. It is read "alimin" (painful) in the genitive and the nominative. As for the genitive, its supposition is: "for them is a punishment of a painful punishment", and if their punishment is from a painful punishment, then their punishment is painful. As for the one who reads it in the nominative, the meaning is: "for them is a painful punishment", and al-Rijz here is intended to mean al-Rijs, which is filth, and the meaning of filth in it is His saying: ﴿and they are given to drink of water like pus﴾ [Ibrahim: 16], and the meaning would be: "for them is a punishment of gulping down filth or drinking filth", so that "min" is explanatory (tabyin) for the punishment.

**God's words: ﴿It is God who subjected the sea to you, so that ships may run upon it by His command, and so that you may seek of His bounty, and perhaps you will be thankful.﴾ ﴿And He subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, all of it from Him. Surely in that are signs for a people who reflect.﴾ ﴿Say to those who believe: forgive those who do not look forward to the Days of God, so that He may recompense a people for what they have earned.﴾ ﴿Whoever does righteousness, it is for his own soul, and whoever does evil, it is against it. Then to your Lord you will be returned.﴾**

Know that God mentioned, as evidence, the manner in which ships run upon the surface of the sea. This does not come about except through the subjection of three things:

First: the winds, which blow according to what is desired.

Second: the creation of the surface of the water with the smoothness on which ships glide.

Third: the creation of wood in a form that remains floating on the surface of the water and does not sink into it.

No one among mankind has power over these three conditions, so there must be an originator who has power over them, and He is God, glorified and exalted. As for His words, ﴿and so that you may seek of His bounty﴾, their meaning is either through trade, or by diving for pearls and coral, or for the sake of extracting fresh meat.

[p. 226]

Then God said: ﴿And He subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, all of it from Him﴾. The meaning is that, had God not held the bodies of the heavens and the earth in their places and their spaces, no benefit would have been obtained. For if the earth were descending or ascending, no benefit could be gained from it. And if the earth were made of gold, silver or iron, no benefit could be gained either. All of this we have already explained. If it is asked: what is the meaning of ﴿from Him﴾ in His words ﴿all of it from Him﴾? We say: its meaning is that it is in the position of a circumstantial clause (ḥāl). The meaning is that He subjected these things while they exist from Him and come into being from Him, that is, He is their Creator and Originator by His power and wisdom, and then He subjects them to His creation. The author of al-Kashshaf (al-Zamakhshari) said: Salamah ibn Muharib read (minhu) so that minhu is the subject of sakhkhara (subjected) by way of metaphorical attribution, or it is the predicate of an omitted subject, meaning: that is from Him, or it is from Him.

Know that when God taught His servants the proofs of tawhid (affirmation of God's oneness), power and wisdom, He followed that with teaching noble character and praiseworthy conduct, by His words: ﴿Say to those who believe: forgive those who do not look forward to the Days of God﴾. By "those who do not look forward to the Days of God" is meant the disbelievers. The exegetes differed concerning the occasion of revelation of this verse. Ibn Abbas said: ﴿Say to those who believe﴾ refers to Umar, and ﴿forgive those who do not look forward to the Days of God﴾ refers to Abdullah ibn Ubayy. This is because they alighted during the expedition against Banu al-Mustaliq at a well called al-Muraysi'. Abdullah sent his servant to draw water, but he was slow in returning. When he came, Abdullah said to him: "What delayed you?" He said: "The servant of Umar sat at the edge of the well and did not let anyone draw water until he had filled the water-skins of the Prophet (ﷺ) and the water-skins of Abu Bakr, and filled some for his master." Abdullah said: "We and these people are only like what is said: fatten your dog and it will devour you." This statement reached Umar, so he took up his sword intending to go to him, and God revealed this verse. Muqatil said: a man from the disbelievers of Quraysh insulted Umar in Mecca, and he resolved to strike him, so God commanded pardon and forbearance, and revealed this verse.

Maymun ibn Mihran narrated that Finhas the Jew, when God revealed His words ﴿Who is it that will lend to God a goodly loan?﴾ [al-Baqarah: 245], said: "The Lord of Muhammad has become needy." Umar heard of this, took up his sword and set out in pursuit of him. The Prophet (ﷺ) sent for him until he was brought back.

As for His words, ﴿those who do not look forward to the Days of God﴾, Ibn Abbas said: they do not hope for God's reward, nor do they fear His punishment, nor do they dread the like of the punishment of the past nations. We have explained the meaning of "the Days of God" at His words ﴿and remind them of the Days of God﴾. Most exegetes say that this verse is abrogated (mansukh, i.e. superseded by a later ruling through naskh). They said this because forgiveness would include not killing them, and when God commanded this fighting, it constituted abrogation. The more likely view is that it should be taken to mean abstaining from disputing over trivial matters, and overlooking the hurtful words and offensive deeds that come from them.

* * *

Then God said: ﴿so that He may recompense a people for what they have earned﴾, that is, so that He may repay with forgiveness a people who do good. If it is asked: what is the point of the indefinite form in His words ﴿so that He may recompense a people﴾, when the intended people are the believers mentioned in His words ﴿Say to those who believe﴾? We say: the indefinite form indicates the magnification of their standing, as if it were said: so that He may recompense a people, and what a people, whose character is to pardon evil deeds, to overlook harmful acts, to bear hardship and to swallow what is disliked. Others said: the meaning of the verse is: "Say to the believers: let them overlook the disbelievers, so that God may recompense the disbelievers for what they have earned of sin." It is as if it were said to them: "Do not requite them yourselves until We requite them." Then He mentioned the general rule, saying: ﴿Whoever does righteousness, it is for his own soul﴾, which is an example God set for those who forgive, ﴿and whoever does evil, it is against it﴾, an example He set for the disbelievers who used to proceed to harm the Messenger and the believers and to do what is not lawful. God thus explained that righteous deeds bring great benefit to their doer, and evil deeds bring harm to their doer, and that He commanded this and forbade that for the benefit of the servant, not for any benefit that returns to Him. This is an encouragement from Him toward righteous deeds and a deterrent from vain deeds.

**Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on Surah 45, verses 18–21:**

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We certainly gave the Children of Israel the Scripture, and judgment, and prophethood, and provided for them of the good things, and preferred them over the worlds﴾. ﴿And We gave them clear proofs of the matter, and they did not differ except after knowledge had come to them, out of envy among themselves. Indeed your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that in which they used to differ﴾. ﴿Then We placed you on a path of the matter, so follow it and do not follow the desires of those who do not know﴾. ﴿Indeed, they will never avail you against Allah at all. And indeed, the wrongdoers are allies of one another, while Allah is the ally of the righteous﴾. ﴿This is evidence for mankind, and guidance and mercy for a people who are certain﴾. ﴿Or do those who commit evil deeds think that We will make them like those who believe and do righteous deeds, equal in their living and their dying? Evil is what they judge﴾.

Know that He, exalted is He, explained that He bestowed many blessings upon the Children of Israel, even though disagreement arose among them out of transgression and envy. The purpose is to show that the way of his people is like the way of those who came before them.

Know that blessings are of two kinds: blessings of religion and blessings of the worldly life. The blessings of religion are superior to the blessings of the worldly life. Therefore Allah, exalted is He, began with mention of the blessings of religion, saying: ﴿And We certainly gave the Children of Israel the Scripture, and judgment, and prophethood﴾. The most likely view is that each of these three must be distinct from the others. As for ﴿the Scripture﴾, it is the Torah. As for ﴿judgment﴾, there are several interpretations: it may mean knowledge and wisdom; it may mean knowledge of the distinguishing of judgments; and it may mean knowing the rulings of Allah, exalted is He, which is the science of fiqh (jurisprudence). As for prophethood, it is well known. As for the blessings of the worldly life, they are what is meant by His saying: ﴿and provided for them of the good things﴾, because He, exalted is He, expanded their provision in this world, so He made them inherit the wealth and dwellings of the people of Pharaoh, then He sent down upon them the manna and the quail. When Allah, exalted is He, explained that He had given them a generous share of both the blessings of religion and the blessings of the worldly life, He said: ﴿and preferred them over the worlds﴾, meaning that they were greater in rank and more elevated in distinction than others in their time. For this reason the exegetes said: the meaning is, "preferred them over the worlds of their time."

* * *

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And We gave them clear proofs of the matter﴾. Regarding this there are several interpretations:

The first: He gave them clear proofs of the matter, that is, proofs concerning the affairs of the world.

The second: Ibn Abbas said: it means He made clear to them, concerning the affair of the Prophet (ﷺ), that he would migrate from Tihama to Yathrib, and that his helpers would be the people of Yathrib.

The third: The meaning of ﴿clear proofs﴾ is compelling miracles as evidence for the truth of their prophethood. The intended meaning is the miracles of Musa (peace be upon him).

[Page 228]

* * *

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿they did not differ except after knowledge had come to them, out of envy among themselves﴾. This is explained in the Surah ﴿Ha Mim 'Ayn Sin Qaf﴾. The purpose of mentioning this statement is to express astonishment at this condition, because the arrival of knowledge necessitates the removal of disagreement, yet here the arrival of knowledge became the cause of disagreement arising. This is because their aim from knowledge was not knowledge itself; rather, what they intended was seeking leadership and precedence. Then there are possibilities here: it may mean that they knew and then were obstinate. It may also mean by "knowledge" the indication that leads to knowledge, and the meaning would be that He placed the proofs and clear evidences which, had they reflected upon them, they would have recognized the truth; but out of envy and obstinacy they differed and openly displayed conflict.

* * *

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that in which they used to differ﴾. The meaning is that the wrongdoer should not be deceived by the blessings of the worldly life, for even if they equal or exceed the blessings of the one who is in the right, he will see in the Hereafter what will grieve him. This is like a warning to them. When Allah, exalted is He, explained that they turned away from the truth out of transgression and envy, He commanded His Messenger (ﷺ) to turn away from that way, to hold fast to the truth, and to have no aim except the manifestation of the truth and the establishment of sincerity. So He said: ﴿Then We placed you on a path of the matter﴾, that is, on a way and method of the religious affair. So follow your law, which is established by proofs and clear evidences, and do not follow what has no proof behind it from the desires of the ignorant and their religions, which are based on desires and ignorance. Al-Kalbi said: The chiefs of Quraysh said to the Prophet (ﷺ) while he was in Mecca: "Return to the religion of your fathers, for they were better than you and older." So Allah, exalted is He, revealed this verse.

* * *

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, they will never avail you against Allah at all﴾, that is, if you were to incline toward their false religions and thus became deserving of punishment, they would not be able to ward off the punishment of Allah from you. Then He explained that the wrongdoers support one another in this world and in the Hereafter, and that they have no ally who benefits them in bringing reward or removing punishment. As for the God-fearing and guided, Allah is their Ally and Helper, and they are His allies. How clear is the difference between the two kinds of allegiance! When Allah, exalted is He, had explained these lasting and beneficial clarifications, He said: ﴿This is evidence for mankind, and guidance and mercy for a people who are certain﴾. We have explained this at the end of Surah al-A'raf. The meaning is: this Qur'an is evidence for mankind. He made the healing clarifications and sufficient proofs it contains like insights in the hearts, just as He placed life and spirit in the rest of the verses. It is guidance from misguidance, and mercy from punishment, for whoever believes and is certain. When Allah, exalted is He, had explained the difference between the wrongdoers and the God-fearing from one aspect that has preceded, He explained the difference between them from another aspect, saying: ﴿Or do those who commit evil deeds think that We will make them like those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾. In this there are several discussions:

The first discussion: ﴿Am﴾ (or) is a word established to ask about something when it is coordinated with something else, whether that coordinated element is mentioned or implied. The implied sense here is: "Do the polytheists know this, or do they suppose that We will take charge of them as We take charge of the God-fearing?"

The second discussion: ﴿al-ijtirah﴾ (committing) means earning, and from it comes "al-jawarih" (limbs, organs of acquisition). It is said: "Fulan is the jarihah of his family," meaning their earner. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And He knows what you have earned by day﴾ [al-An'am: 60].

The third discussion: Al-Kalbi said: This verse was revealed concerning Ali, Hamzah, and Abu Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah, may Allah be pleased with them, and concerning three of the polytheists: Utbah, Shaybah, and al-Walid ibn Utbah. They said to the believers: "By Allah, you are of no consequence. If what you say were true, then our condition in the Hereafter would be better than yours, just as we are better off than you in this world." So Allah rejected this statement and explained that it is impossible for the condition of the obedient believer to be equal to that of the disobedient unbeliever in the degrees of reward and the ranks of felicity.

Know that the word ﴿hasiba﴾ (supposed) requires two objects:

One of them is the pronoun mentioned in His saying: ﴿that We will make them﴾.

The second is the kaf (like) in His saying: ﴿like those who believe﴾. The meaning is: "Do these committers of evil suppose that We will make them like those who believe?"

A parallel to this is His saying: ﴿Is one who was a believer like one who was defiantly disobedient? They are not equal﴾ [as-Sajdah: 18], and His saying: ﴿Indeed, We will support Our messengers and those who believe in the life of this world and on the day when the witnesses stand, the day when their excuse will not benefit the wrongdoers, and for them is the curse and for them is the worst abode﴾ [Ghafir: 51–52], and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Shall We treat the Muslims like the criminals? What is wrong with you? How do you judge?﴾ [al-Qalam: 35–36], and His saying: ﴿Or shall We make those who believe and do righteous deeds like the corrupters on earth? Or shall We make the God-fearing like the wicked?﴾ [Sad: 28].

* * *

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿equal in their living and their dying﴾. In this there are issues:

The first issue: Hamzah, al-Kisa'i, and Hafs from Asim read ﴿sawa'an﴾ (equal) in the accusative, while the rest read it in the nominative. Abu Ubayd preferred the accusative. As for the reading in the nominative, it is that His saying ﴿their living and their dying﴾ is a subject (mubtada'), and the clause, in the sense of a single noun, is in a position of accusative by way of substitution (badal) for the second object of ﴿We make﴾, which is the kaf in ﴿like those who believe﴾. A parallel to this is His saying: "I thought Zayd, his father is departing." As for the reading in the accusative, the author of al-Kashshaf said: He treated ﴿sawa'an﴾ as if it were ﴿mustawiyan﴾ (equal), so ﴿their living and their dying﴾ took the subject role (fa'iliyyah), and it was singular and not a clause. And whoever reads ﴿wa-mamatuhum﴾ (and their dying) in the accusative makes ﴿their living and their dying﴾ two adverbs of time and place, like "the arrival of the pilgrim" and "the rising of the star," meaning: equal in their living and in their dying. Abu Ali said: Whoever puts ﴿sawa'an﴾ in the accusative makes "their living and their dying" a substitute for the pronoun in the accusative in ﴿We make them﴾, so the sense becomes: "that We make their living and their dying equal." He said: It is also permissible to make it a circumstantial accusative (hal), and the second object is the kaf in ﴿like those who﴾.

The second issue: They differed about the meaning of ﴿their living and their dying﴾. Mujahid said, from Ibn Abbas: The meaning is, "Do they suppose that their life and death are like the life and death of the believers? No indeed. They live as unbelievers and die as unbelievers, while the believers live as believers and die as believers. This is because while the believer is in this world, Allah is his Ally, the believers are his helpers, and the proof of Allah is with him; the unbeliever is the opposite of this, as He mentioned in His saying: ﴿And indeed, the wrongdoers are allies of one another﴾. And at the approach of death, the condition of the believer is what He mentioned in His saying: ﴿those whom the angels take in death while they are good, saying, 'Peace be upon you; enter Paradise'﴾ [an-Nahl: 32], and the condition of the unbeliever is what He mentioned in His saying: ﴿those whom the angels take in death while they are wronging themselves﴾ [an-Nahl: 28]. As for on the Day of Resurrection, He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Faces that Day will be bright, laughing, rejoicing; and faces that Day will have upon them dust, covered with darkness﴾ [Abasa: 38–41]. This is an indication of the difference between the two conditions."

The second interpretation of the verse is that the meaning is a denial that they would be equal in death as they were equal in life. This is because the believer and the unbeliever may be equal in their life in health, provision, and sufficiency; indeed the unbeliever may be better off than the believer. The difference between them only becomes apparent at death.

The third interpretation is that His saying ﴿equal their living and their dying﴾ is a new (independent) statement, meaning that the living and dying of the evildoers is equal, and likewise the living and dying of the good-doers; each dies according to how he lived. Then He, exalted is He, explicitly denied that equalization, saying: ﴿Evil is what they judge﴾, and this is clear.

* * *

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that in which they used to differ﴾. The meaning is that the wrongdoer should not be deceived by the blessings of the worldly life, for even if they equal or exceed the blessings of the one who is in the right, he will see in the Hereafter what will grieve him. This is like a warning to them. When Allah, exalted is He, explained that they turned away from the truth out of transgression and envy, He commanded His Messenger (ﷺ) to turn away from that way, to hold fast to the truth, and to have no aim except the manifestation of the truth and the establishment of sincerity. So He said: ﴿Then We placed you on a path of the matter﴾, that is, on a way and method of the religious affair. * * *

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, they will never avail you against Allah at all﴾, that is, if you were to incline toward their false religions and thus became deserving of punishment, they would not be able to ward off the punishment of Allah from you. Then He explained that the wrongdoers support one another in this world and in the Hereafter, and that they have no ally who benefits them in bringing reward or removing punishment. As for the God-fearing and guided, Allah is their Ally and Helper, and they are His allies. How clear is the difference between the two kinds of allegiance! When Allah, exalted is He, had explained these lasting and beneficial clarifications, He said: ﴿This is evidence for mankind, and guidance and mercy for a people who are certain﴾. We have explained this at the end of Surah al-A'raf. The meaning is: this Qur'an is evidence for mankind. He made the healing clarifications and sufficient proofs it contains like insights in the hearts, just as He placed life and spirit in the rest of the verses. They said to the believers: "By Allah, you are of no consequence. If what you say were true, then our condition in the Hereafter would be better than yours, just as we are better off than you in this world." So Allah rejected this statement and explained that it is impossible for the condition of the obedient believer to be equal to that of the disobedient unbeliever in the degrees of reward and the ranks of felicity.

Know that the word ﴿hasiba﴾ (supposed) requires two objects:

One of them is the pronoun mentioned in His saying: ﴿that We will make them﴾.

The second is the kaf (like) in His saying: ﴿like those who believe﴾. The meaning is: "Do these committers of evil suppose that We will make them like those who believe?"

A parallel to this is His saying: ﴿Is one who was a believer like one who was defiantly disobedient? They are not equal﴾ [as-Sajdah: 18], and His saying: ﴿Indeed, We will support Our messengers and those who believe in the life of this world and on the day when the witnesses stand, the day when their excuse will not benefit the wrongdoers, and for them is the curse and for them is the worst abode﴾ [Ghafir: 51–52], and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Shall We treat the Muslims like the criminals? What is wrong with you? How do you judge?﴾ [al-Qalam: 35–36], and His saying: ﴿Or shall We make those who believe and do righteous deeds like the corrupters on earth? Or shall We make the God-fearing like the wicked?﴾ [Sad: 28].

* * *

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿equal in their living and their dying﴾. In this there are issues:

The first issue: Hamzah, al-Kisa'i, and Hafs from Asim read ﴿sawa'an﴾ (equal) in the accusative, while the rest read it in the nominative. Abu Ubayd preferred the accusative. As for the reading in the nominative, it is that His saying ﴿their living and their dying﴾ is a subject (mubtada'), and the clause, in the sense of a single noun, is in a position of accusative by way of substitution (badal) for the second object of ﴿We make﴾, which is the kaf in ﴿like those who believe﴾. A parallel to this is His saying: "I thought Zayd, his father is departing." As for the reading in the accusative, the author of al-Kashshaf said: He treated ﴿sawa'an﴾ as if it were ﴿mustawiyan﴾ (equal), so ﴿their living and their dying﴾ took the subject role (fa'iliyyah), and it was singular and not a clause. And whoever reads ﴿wa-mamatuhum﴾ (and their dying) in the accusative makes ﴿their living and their dying﴾ two adverbs of time and place, like "the arrival of the pilgrim" and "the rising of the star," meaning: equal in their living and in their dying. He said: It is also permissible to make it a circumstantial accusative (hal), and the second object is the kaf in ﴿like those who﴾.

The second issue: They differed about the meaning of ﴿their living and their dying﴾. Mujahid said, from Ibn Abbas: The meaning is, "Do they suppose that their life and death are like the life and death of the believers? No indeed. They live as unbelievers and die as unbelievers, while the believers live as believers and die as believers. This is because while the believer is in this world, Allah is his Ally, the believers are his helpers, and the proof of Allah is with him; the unbeliever is the opposite of this, as He mentioned in His saying: ﴿And indeed, the wrongdoers are allies of one another﴾. And at the approach of death, the condition of the believer is what He mentioned in His saying: ﴿those whom the angels take in death while they are good, saying, 'Peace be upon you; enter Paradise'﴾ [an-Nahl: 32], and the condition of the unbeliever is what He mentioned in His saying: ﴿those whom the angels take in death while they are wronging themselves﴾ [an-Nahl: 28]. As for on the Day of Resurrection, He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Faces that Day will be bright, laughing, rejoicing; and faces that Day will have upon them dust, covered with darkness﴾ [Abasa: 38–41]. This is an indication of the difference between the two conditions."

The second interpretation of the verse is that the meaning is a denial that they would be equal in death as they were equal in life. This is because the believer and the unbeliever may be equal in their life in health, provision, and sufficiency; indeed the unbeliever may be better off than the believer. The difference between them only becomes apparent at death.

The third interpretation is that His saying ﴿equal their living and their dying﴾ is a new (independent) statement, meaning that the living and dying of the evildoers is equal, and likewise the living and dying of the good-doers; each dies according to how he lived. Then He, exalted is He, explicitly denied that equalization, saying: ﴿Evil is what they judge﴾, and this is clear.

When Allah, exalted is He, had explained the difference between the wrongdoers and the God-fearing from one aspect that has preceded, He explained the difference between them from another aspect, saying: ﴿Or do those who commit evil deeds think that We will make them like those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾. In this there are several discussions:

The first discussion: ﴿Am﴾ (or) is a word established to ask about something when it is coordinated with something else, whether that coordinated element is mentioned or implied. The implied sense here is: "Do the polytheists know this, or do they suppose that We will take charge of them as We take charge of the God-fearing?"

The second discussion: ﴿al-ijtirah﴾ (committing) means earning, and from it comes "al-jawarih" (limbs, organs of acquisition). It is said: "Fulan is the jarihah of his family," meaning their earner. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And He knows what you have earned by day﴾ [al-An'am: 60].

The third discussion: Al-Kalbi said: This verse was revealed concerning Ali, Hamzah, and Abu Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah, may Allah be pleased with them, and concerning three of the polytheists: Utbah, Shaybah, and al-Walid ibn Utbah. They said to the believers: "By Allah, you are of no consequence. If what you say were true, then our condition in the Hereafter would be better than yours, just as we are better off than you in this world." So Allah rejected this statement and explained that it is impossible for the condition of the obedient believer to be equal to that of the disobedient unbeliever in the degrees of reward and the ranks of felicity.

Know that the word ﴿hasiba﴾ (supposed) requires two objects:

One of them is the pronoun mentioned in His saying: ﴿that We will make them﴾.

The second is the kaf (like) in His saying: ﴿like those who believe﴾. The meaning is: "Do these committers of evil suppose that We will make them like those who believe?"

A parallel to this is His saying: ﴿Is one who was a believer like one who was defiantly disobedient? They are not equal﴾ [as-Sajdah: 18], and His saying: ﴿Indeed, We will support Our messengers and those who believe in the life of this world and on the day when the witnesses stand, the day when their excuse will not benefit the wrongdoers, and for them is the curse and for them is the worst abode﴾ [Ghafir: 51–52], and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Shall We treat the Muslims like the criminals? What is wrong with you? How do you judge?﴾ [al-Qalam: 35–36], and His saying: ﴿Or shall We make those who believe and do righteous deeds like the corrupters on earth? Or shall We make the God-fearing like the wicked?﴾ [Sad: 28].

* * *

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿equal in their living and their dying﴾. In this there are issues:

The first issue: Hamzah, al-Kisa'i, and Hafs from Asim read ﴿sawa'an﴾ (equal) in the accusative, while the rest read it in the nominative. Abu Ubayd preferred the accusative. As for the reading in the nominative, it is that His saying ﴿their living and their dying﴾ is a subject (mubtada'), and the clause, in the sense of a single noun, is in a position of accusative by way of substitution (badal) for the second object of ﴿We make﴾, which is the kaf in ﴿like those who believe﴾. A parallel to this is His saying: "I thought Zayd, his father is departing." As for the reading in the accusative, the author of al-Kashshaf said: He treated ﴿sawa'an﴾ as if it were ﴿mustawiyan﴾ (equal), so ﴿their living and their dying﴾ took the subject role (fa'iliyyah), and it was singular and not a clause. And whoever reads ﴿wa-mamatuhum﴾ (and their dying) in the accusative makes ﴿their living and their dying﴾ two adverbs of time and place, like "the arrival of the pilgrim" and "the rising of the star," meaning: equal in their living and in their dying. Abu Ali said: Whoever puts ﴿sawa'an﴾ in the accusative makes "their living and their dying" a substitute for the pronoun in the accusative in ﴿We make them﴾, so the sense becomes: "that We make their living and their dying equal." He said: It is also permissible to make it a circumstantial accusative (hal), and the second object is the kaf in ﴿like those who﴾.

The second issue: They differed about the meaning of ﴿their living and their dying﴾. Mujahid said, from Ibn Abbas: The meaning is, "Do they suppose that their life and death are like the life and death of the believers? No indeed. They live as unbelievers and die as unbelievers, while the believers live as believers and die as believers. This is because while the believer is in this world, Allah is his Ally, the believers are his helpers, and the proof of Allah is with him; the unbeliever is the opposite of this, as He mentioned in His saying: ﴿And indeed, the wrongdoers are allies of one another﴾. And at the approach of death, the condition of the believer is what He mentioned in His saying: ﴿those whom the angels take in death while they are good, saying, 'Peace be upon you; enter Paradise'﴾ [an-Nahl: 32], and the condition of the unbeliever is what He mentioned in His saying: ﴿those whom the angels take in death while they are wronging themselves﴾ [an-Nahl: 28]. As for on the Day of Resurrection, He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Faces that Day will be bright, laughing, rejoicing; and faces that Day will have upon them dust, covered with darkness﴾ [Abasa: 38–41]. This is an indication of the difference between the two conditions."

The second interpretation of the verse is that the meaning is a denial that they would be equal in death as they were equal in life. This is because the believer and the unbeliever may be equal in their life in health, provision, and sufficiency; indeed the unbeliever may be better off than the believer. The difference between them only becomes apparent at death.

The third interpretation is that His saying ﴿equal their living and their dying﴾ is a new (independent) statement, meaning that the living and dying of the evildoers is equal, and likewise the living and dying of the good-doers; each dies according to how he lived. Then He, exalted is He, explicitly denied that equalization, saying: ﴿Evil is what they judge﴾, and this is clear.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 45, verses 22–26:

The Exalted said: ﴿And God created the heavens and the earth in truth, and so that every soul may be recompensed for what it has earned, and they will not be wronged.﴾ ﴿Have you seen him who takes his desire as his god, and God has led him astray knowingly, and has sealed his hearing and his heart, and placed a veil over his sight? Who then will guide him after God? Will you not take heed?﴾ ﴿And they say, "There is nothing but our life of this world: we die and we live, and nothing destroys us except time." They have no knowledge of that; they only conjecture.﴾ ﴿And when Our clear signs are recited to them, their argument is only that they say, "Bring our fathers, if you are truthful."﴾ ﴿Say: "God gives you life, then causes you to die, then will gather you to the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt," but most people do not know.﴾

Know that when He, the Exalted, pronounced the judgement that the believer is not equal to the disbeliever in the degrees of felicity, He followed it with the manifest proof of the soundness of this judgement, and said: ﴿And God created the heavens and the earth in truth.﴾ Had there been no resurrection, this creation would not have been in truth but in falsehood. For when He, the Exalted, created the wrongdoer and gave him power over the weak oppressed one, and then does not avenge the oppressed upon the oppressor, He would be a wrongdoer; and if He were a wrongdoer, it would be invalid that ﴿God created the heavens and the earth in truth.﴾ The full establishment of these proofs is mentioned at the beginning of Surah Yunus. The Qadi (al-Qadi) said: this verse indicates that within God's power is something which, if it occurred, would be an injustice. This is not valid except according to the doctrine of the Mujbira (determinists), who say: if He does whatever He wills, it is not injustice; and according to the view of those who say that He is not described as having the power to do injustice. Our companions (the Ash'aris) answered him that what is meant is doing something which, if anyone else did it, would be injustice, just as what is meant by trial and testing is doing something which, if anyone else did it, would be a trial and a test.

And His saying ﴿and so that﴾ (wa-li-tujzā) has two possibilities:

The first: it is coordinated with His saying ﴿in truth﴾, so the meaning is: God created the heavens and the earth for the sake of manifesting the truth, and so that every soul may be recompensed.

The second: the conjunction is with something omitted, and the meaning is: God created the heavens and the earth in truth so that by them He would indicate His power, ﴿and so that every soul may be recompensed.﴾ The meaning is that the purpose of creating this world is the manifestation of justice and mercy, and this is not complete except when the resurrection and the Last Day take place and there is a difference in degrees and ranks between the righteous and the falsifiers.

Then the Exalted returned to describing the state of the disbelievers and their ugly ways, and said: ﴿Have you seen him who takes his desire as his god?﴾ That is, they abandoned following guidance and turned to following desire, so they worshipped desire as a man worships his god. It has been read (ālihatahu hawāhu, "its gods are his desires"): whenever his disposition inclined toward something, he followed it and went after it, so it is as if he had taken his desire as many gods, worshipping one of them at each time.

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And God has led him astray knowingly﴾, that is, with knowledge that the essence of his soul does not accept righteousness. Its parallel on the side of honour is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿God knows best where to place His message﴾ [al-An'am: 124]. The truth of the matter is that the essences of human souls differ: some are radiant, luminous, lofty and divine, and some are turbid, dark, low, and greatly inclined to bodily desires. He, the Exalted, deals with each of them according to what suits their essence and quiddity. This is what is meant by His saying ﴿and God has led him astray knowingly﴾ concerning those who are rejected, and by His saying ﴿God knows best where to place His message﴾ concerning those who are accepted.

* * *

Then He said: ﴿and has sealed his hearing and his heart, and placed a veil over his sight.﴾ His saying ﴿and God has led him astray knowingly﴾ is what is mentioned in His saying ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve﴾ up to His saying ﴿they do not believe﴾. And His saying ﴿and has sealed his hearing and his heart, and placed a veil over his sight﴾ is what is meant by His saying ﴿God has sealed upon their hearts and upon their hearing, and over their sight is a veil﴾. All of this has already been explained in detail in Surah al-Baqarah. The difference between the two verses is that in this verse He mentioned hearing before the heart, while in Surah al-Baqarah He mentioned the heart before hearing. The distinction is that a person may hear a speech and an effect settles in his heart from it, as when a group of disbelievers used to tell people that the Prophet (ﷺ) was a poet and a soothsayer, and that he sought kingship and leadership. Listeners, when they heard this, hated him and their hearts recoiled from him. As for the disbelievers of Makkah, they hated him in their hearts because of intense envy, so they used to listen to him, but if they heard his speech they would not understand from it anything beneficial. In the first case, the effect rises from the body to the essence of the soul; in the second case, the effect descends from the essence of the soul to the seat of the body. Since the two categories differ, God, the Exalted, has indeed directed to both categories by these two orders that we have pointed out.

When God, the Exalted, mentioned this speech, He said: ﴿Who then will guide him after God?﴾ That is, after God has led him astray. ﴿Will you not take heed?﴾ O people. Al-Wahidi said: with this verse, the Qadariyya have no excuse or stratagem left, because God, the Exalted, has explicitly stated His preventing them from guidance when He informed that He sealed the hearing, heart and sight of this disbeliever. I say: this debate has already been thoroughly preceded in the beginning of Surah al-Baqarah.

Know that after this He, the Exalted, related their doubt concerning the denial of the Resurrection and their denial of the all-powerful God. As for their doubt concerning the denial of the Resurrection, it is His saying: ﴿And they say, "There is nothing but our life of this world: we die and we live."﴾ If they say: life precedes death in this world, so the deniers of the Resurrection should have said: "We live and we die." What is the reason for mentioning death before life? We reply: there are several answers.

The first: by His saying ﴿we die﴾ is meant the state in which they were drops of semen in the loins of fathers and the wombs of mothers, and by His saying ﴿we live﴾ is meant what occurred after that in this world.

The second: we die ourselves, and we live through the survival of our children.

The third: some die and some live.

The fourth, which came to mind when writing this passage: He, the Exalted, mentioned life first, saying ﴿and they say, "There is nothing but our life of this world,"﴾ then after it He said ﴿we die and we live,﴾ meaning that among that life there is what death befalls, and that is in the case of those who have died; and there is what death has not yet befallen, and that is in the case of the living who have not yet died.

As for their doubt concerning denying the Creator who acts by choice, it is their saying: ﴿nothing destroys us except time.﴾ That is, the generation of persons occurs only through the movements of the spheres, which necessitate the mixtures of natures. When those mixtures occur in a particular way, life results; and when they occur in another way, death results. So what causes life and death is the influences of natures and the movements of the spheres, and there is no need in this matter to establish an agent who chooses. Thus this group combined the denial of God with the denial of resurrection and the Last Day.

* * *

Then the Exalted said: ﴿And they have no knowledge of that; they only conjecture.﴾ The meaning is that before consideration and knowing the proof, all possibilities remain open: what they said may be the case, and its opposite is also possible, namely that the belief in resurrection and the Last Day is true, and that the belief in the existence of a wise God is true. They did not mention any weak or strong doubt that this second possibility is false; rather, that first possibility occurred to them, so they affirmed it and insisted upon it without any argument or evidence. It is therefore established that there is no knowledge, no certainty, and no conviction in the soundness of the view they adopted, but only conjecture and speculation and the inclination of the heart towards it without any valid reason. This verse is among the strongest proofs that a claim without argument or evidence is false and corrupt, and that following conjecture and speculation is abhorrent in the sight of God, the Exalted.

* * *

Then the Exalted said: ﴿And when Our clear signs are recited to them, their argument is only that they say, "Bring our fathers, if you are truthful."﴾ In this there are issues:

The first issue: it has been read ḥujjatuhum (their argument), with the nominative, by placing the predicate of kāna before it.

The second issue: he called their saying an argument for several reasons:

The first: because in their opinion it is an argument.

The second: what is meant by "their argument was" is this, though it is in no way an argument, as in the line: "Their greeting among them is a painful striking" [meaning there is no greeting among them, since striking contradicts greeting].

The third: they mentioned it in the context of arguing with it.

The third issue: their argument against the resurrection was that they said: if that is correct, then bring our fathers who have died, so that they may bear witness for us to the soundness of the resurrection.

Know that this doubt is very weak, because not everything that does not occur at present must be impossible to occur. For the coming into being of each one of us was non-existent from eternity until the time when we came into being. If the non-occurrence at a specific time indicated the impossibility of occurrence, then our non-occurrence in that manner would also be impossible, and that is invalid by consensus.

* * *

Then the Exalted said: ﴿Say: "God gives you life, then causes you to die, then will gather you to the Day of Resurrection."﴾ If it is said: this statement is mentioned as a response to the one who says: ﴿There is nothing but our life of this world: we die and we live, and nothing destroys us except time.﴾ This speaker denied the existence of God and the existence of the Day of Resurrection, so how is it permissible to refute his speech by saying ﴿Say: "God gives you life, then causes you to die"﴾? Is this not establishing a thing by itself, which is invalid? We reply: He, the Exalted, has mentioned in the Qur'an, many times and in various ways, the argument from the origination of animals and humans to the existence of a wise Agent. So His saying here ﴿Say: "God gives you life"﴾ is an indication to those proofs which He has clarified and made plain many times. The purpose of mentioning this statement is not to establish God by the word of God, but rather to draw attention to what is the true, decisive proof in reality itself.

Since it is established that giving life is from God, the Exalted, and it is established that the restoration is like the first giving of life, and it is established that the one capable of a thing is capable of its like, it is established that He, the Exalted, is capable of the restoration. It is established that the restoration is possible in itself, and it is established that the all-powerful, wise One has informed of the time of its occurrence, so it becomes necessary to be certain that it is true.

* * *

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿then will gather you to the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt,﴾ it is a reference to what was mentioned in the preceding verse, namely that His being just, the Creator in truth, exalted above injustice and oppression, necessitates the soundness of the resurrection and the Last Day.

Then the Exalted said: ﴿but most people do not know.﴾ That is: but most people do not know the indication of the origination of humans, animals and plants of the existence of the all-powerful, wise God; and they also do not know that since He, the Exalted, was able to originate creation at the beginning, it is necessary that He be able to restore it a second time.
