When God, the Exalted, mentioned this speech, He said: ﴿Who then will guide him after God?﴾ That is, after God has led him astray. ﴿Will you not take heed?﴾ O people. Al-Wahidi said: with this verse, the Qadariyya have no excuse or stratagem left, because God, the Exalted, has explicitly stated His preventing them from guidance when He informed that He sealed the hearing, heart and sight of this disbeliever. I say: this debate has already been thoroughly preceded in the beginning of Surah al-Baqarah.

Know that after this He, the Exalted, related their doubt concerning the denial of the Resurrection and their denial of the all-powerful God. As for their doubt concerning the denial of the Resurrection, it is His saying: ﴿And they say, "There is nothing but our life of this world: we die and we live."﴾ If they say: life precedes death in this world, so the deniers of the Resurrection should have said: "We live and we die." What is the reason for mentioning death before life? We reply: there are several answers.

The first: by His saying ﴿we die﴾ is meant the state in which they were drops of semen in the loins of fathers and the wombs of mothers, and by His saying ﴿we live﴾ is meant what occurred after that in this world.

The second: we die ourselves, and we live through the survival of our children.

The third: some die and some live.

The fourth, which came to mind when writing this passage: He, the Exalted, mentioned life first, saying ﴿and they say, "There is nothing but our life of this world,"﴾ then after it He said ﴿we die and we live,﴾ meaning that among that life there is what death befalls, and that is in the case of those who have died; and there is what death has not yet befallen, and that is in the case of the living who have not yet died.

As for their doubt concerning denying the Creator who acts by choice, it is their saying: ﴿nothing destroys us except time.﴾ That is, the generation of persons occurs only through the movements of the spheres, which necessitate the mixtures of natures. When those mixtures occur in a particular way, life results; and when they occur in another way, death results. So what causes life and death is the influences of natures and the movements of the spheres, and there is no need in this matter to establish an agent who chooses. Thus this group combined the denial of God with the denial of resurrection and the Last Day.

* * *

Then the Exalted said: ﴿And they have no knowledge of that; they only conjecture.﴾ The meaning is that before consideration and knowing the proof, all possibilities remain open: what they said may be the case, and its opposite is also possible, namely that the belief in resurrection and the Last Day is true, and that the belief in the existence of a wise God is true. They did not mention any weak or strong doubt that this second possibility is false; rather, that first possibility occurred to them, so they affirmed it and insisted upon it without any argument or evidence. It is therefore established that there is no knowledge, no certainty, and no conviction in the soundness of the view they adopted, but only conjecture and speculation and the inclination of the heart towards it without any valid reason. This verse is among the strongest proofs that a claim without argument or evidence is false and corrupt, and that following conjecture and speculation is abhorrent in the sight of God, the Exalted.

* * *

Then the Exalted said: ﴿And when Our clear signs are recited to them, their argument is only that they say, "Bring our fathers, if you are truthful."﴾ In this there are issues:

The first issue: it has been read ḥujjatuhum (their argument), with the nominative, by placing the predicate of kāna before it.

The second issue: he called their saying an argument for several reasons:

The first: because in their opinion it is an argument.

The second: what is meant by "their argument was" is this, though it is in no way an argument, as in the line: "Their greeting among them is a painful striking" [meaning there is no greeting among them, since striking contradicts greeting].

The third: they mentioned it in the context of arguing with it.

The third issue: their argument against the resurrection was that they said: if that is correct, then bring our fathers who have died, so that they may bear witness for us to the soundness of the resurrection.

Know that this doubt is very weak, because not everything that does not occur at present must be impossible to occur. For the coming into being of each one of us was non-existent from eternity until the time when we came into being. If the non-occurrence at a specific time indicated the impossibility of occurrence, then our non-occurrence in that manner would also be impossible, and that is invalid by consensus.

* * *

Then the Exalted said: ﴿Say: "God gives you life, then causes you to die, then will gather you to the Day of Resurrection."﴾ If it is said: this statement is mentioned as a response to the one who says: ﴿There is nothing but our life of this world: we die and we live, and nothing destroys us except time.﴾ This speaker denied the existence of God and the existence of the Day of Resurrection, so how is it permissible to refute his speech by saying ﴿Say: "God gives you life, then causes you to die"﴾? Is this not establishing a thing by itself, which is invalid? We reply: He, the Exalted, has mentioned in the Qur'an, many times and in various ways, the argument from the origination of animals and humans to the existence of a wise Agent. So His saying here ﴿Say: "God gives you life"﴾ is an indication to those proofs which He has clarified and made plain many times. The purpose of mentioning this statement is not to establish God by the word of God, but rather to draw attention to what is the true, decisive proof in reality itself.

Since it is established that giving life is from God, the Exalted, and it is established that the restoration is like the first giving of life, and it is established that the one capable of a thing is capable of its like, it is established that He, the Exalted, is capable of the restoration. It is established that the restoration is possible in itself, and it is established that the all-powerful, wise One has informed of the time of its occurrence, so it becomes necessary to be certain that it is true.

* * *

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿then will gather you to the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt,﴾ it is a reference to what was mentioned in the preceding verse, namely that His being just, the Creator in truth, exalted above injustice and oppression, necessitates the soundness of the resurrection and the Last Day.

Then the Exalted said: ﴿but most people do not know.﴾ That is: but most people do not know the indication of the origination of humans, animals and plants of the existence of the all-powerful, wise God; and they also do not know that since He, the Exalted, was able to originate creation at the beginning, it is necessary that He be able to restore it a second time.

**Verses 27–37**

﴿To God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. And on the day the Hour is established, on that day the falsifiers will lose.﴾ ﴿And you will see every nation kneeling. Every nation will be called to its record: "Today you will be recompensed for what you used to do."﴾ ﴿This is Our record, speaking against you with truth. Indeed, We used to have copies made of what you used to do.﴾ ﴿As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, their Lord will admit them into His mercy. That is the clear triumph.﴾ ﴿As for those who disbelieved: "Were My verses not recited to you? But you were arrogant and were a criminal people."﴾

Know that when God, exalted is He, argued by His being capable of bringing life in the first instance, and by His being capable of bringing life a second time, in the preceding verses, He generalized the proof and said: ﴿To God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth.﴾ That is, to God belongs the power over all possible things, whether they are of the heavens or of the earth. When it is established that God is capable of all possible things, and it is established that the occurrence of life in this essence is possible (for if it were not possible, it would not have occurred the first time), it follows from these two premises that He, exalted is He, is capable of bringing life a second time.

When God, exalted is He, clarified the possibility of speaking of the Gathering and the Resurrection by these two ways, He mentioned the details of the conditions of the Resurrection. The first of these is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And on the day the Hour is established, on that day the falsifiers will lose.﴾ Concerning this there are several discussions:

The first discussion: the governing element of the accusative in "the day the Hour is established" is "will lose," and "on that day" is a substitute for "the day the Hour is established."

The second discussion: We have mentioned in several places in this book that life, reason and health are, as it were, capital, and the disposal of them in seeking the happiness of the Hereafter proceeds in the manner of a merchant's disposal of his capital in seeking profit. The disbelievers have exhausted themselves in these dispositions, and they found from them nothing but deprivation and abandonment. Thus that, in reality, was the utmost of loss.

Second: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And you will see every nation kneeling.﴾ Al-Layth said: "al-juthuww" is sitting on the knees, as one kneels before a judge. Al-Zajjaj said: "Similar to it is jadha, yajdhu." The author of al-Kashshaf said: "It was also recited as jadhiyah." The lexicographers said: "al-judhuww" is more intense in its bracing than "al-juthuww," because the one who is jadhi is the one who sits on the tips of his toes. It is related from Ibn 'Abbas: "jathiyah" means gathered together, awaiting what will be done with them.

* * *

Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Every nation will be called to its record,﴾ with "every nation" in the nominative as the subject, and "every nation" as a substitute for "every nation" [the earlier one]. His saying "to its record" means to the pages of its deeds. He suffices with the generic noun, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the Book will be placed, and you will see the criminals fearful of what is in it﴾ [al-Kahf: 49]. The apparent meaning is that both believers and disbelievers are included, because of His saying after that: ﴿As for those who believed.﴾

* * *

Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿As for those who disbelieved.﴾ If it is said: kneeling on the knee befits only one who fears, and the believers have no fear on the Day of Resurrection. We say: the one who is righteous and secure may share with the falsifier in such a state until it becomes manifest that he is righteous.

* * *

Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Today you will be recompensed.﴾ The implied meaning is: it will be said to them, "Today you will be recompensed." If it is said: how is the Book attributed to them and to God, exalted is He? We say: there is no contradiction between the two matters. It is "their book" in the sense that it is the book containing their deeds, and it is "God's Book" in the sense that He is the One who commanded the angels to write it. ﴿It speaks against you﴾ means it bears witness against you for what you did, without addition or subtraction. ﴿Indeed, We used to have copies made﴾ — the angels — ﴿of what you used to do﴾, that is, We used to have your deeds written down.

Then He clarified the condition of the obedient, saying: ﴿As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, their Lord will admit them into His mercy. That is the clear triumph.﴾ Concerning this there are several issues:

The first issue: after describing them with faith, He mentioned that they were doing righteous deeds, so it is necessary that doing righteous deeds be different from faith and additional to it.

The second issue: the Mu'tazilites (a theological school) said: He made entry into God's mercy conditional upon their bringing faith and righteous deeds together, and what is conditional upon two matters together is nonexistent when one of them is absent. So when righteous deeds are absent, it is necessary that the triumph of Paradise not be attained. Our answer: making a ruling conditional upon an attribute does not indicate the absence of the ruling when the attribute is absent.

The third issue: He called the reward "mercy," and mercy can properly be called by this name only when it is not obligatory. Therefore it is necessary that reward not be obligatory upon God, exalted is He.

* * *

Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿As for those who disbelieved: "Were My verses not recited to you? But you were arrogant and were a criminal people."﴾ Concerning this there are several issues:

The first issue: God mentioned the believers and the disbelievers and did not mention a third category. This indicates that the doctrine of the Mu'tazilites, that of an intermediate position (between belief and disbelief), is false.

The second issue: He gave as the reason for the deserving of punishment that His verses were recited to them and they were arrogant toward accepting them. This indicates that the deserving of punishment does not occur except after the coming of the Law (shar'), and that indicates that obligations are not obligatory except through the Law, contrary to what the Mu'tazilites say, that some obligations may be obligatory by reason ('aql).

The third issue: the answer to "as for" (amma) is omitted, and the implied meaning is: "As for those who disbelieved, it will be said to them: 'Were My verses not recited to you? But you were arrogant'" toward accepting the truth, "and you were a criminal people"? If they say: how is it good to describe the disbeliever as a criminal, in the context of censure and blame directed at him? We say: its meaning is that they, despite being disbelievers, were not upright in their own religions; rather they were corrupt in that religion. And God knows best.

* * *

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when it was said, "Indeed, the promise of God is true, and the Hour, there is no doubt in it," you said, "We do not know what the Hour is; we only assume an assumption, and we are not certain."﴾ ﴿And there will appear to them the evils of what they did, and there will befall them what they used to mock.﴾ ﴿And it will be said, "Today We forget you as you forgot the meeting of this your day. Your refuge is the Fire, and you have no helpers."﴾ ﴿That is because you took the signs of God in mockery, and the worldly life deceived you. So today they will not be brought out of it, nor will they be allowed to seek to please Him.﴾ ﴿So to God belongs praise, Lord of the heavens and Lord of the earth, Lord of the worlds.﴾ ﴿And to Him belongs grandeur in the heavens and the earth, and He is the Mighty, the Wise.﴾ Concerning this there are several issues:

The first issue: "and the Hour" was recited in both the nominative and the accusative. Al-Zajjaj said: whoever reads it in the accusative makes it conjoined to "the promise," and whoever reads it in the nominative does so in the sense of "and it was said: 'the Hour, there is no doubt in it.'" Al-Akhfash said: the nominative is better in meaning and more common in Arabic speech when it comes after the predicate of "inna," because it is a sentence standing on its own after the first sentence has been completed in full.

The second issue: God, exalted is He, related about the disbelievers that when it was said to them that God's promise of reward and punishment is true, and that the Hour is coming, there is no doubt in it, they said: "We do not know what the Hour is; we only assume an assumption, and we are not certain."

I say: the more probable view is that the people were, on this matter, of two positions. Among them were those who were definitively denying resurrection and the Hour, and they are those whom God mentioned in the preceding verse by His saying: ﴿And they said: there is nothing but our worldly life.﴾ And among them were those who were doubtful and bewildered about it, because from the great amount they had heard from the Messenger (ﷺ), and from the great amount of evidence they had heard in support of its truth, they became doubtful about it. These are the ones whom this verse intends. What indicates this is that He, exalted is He, related the doctrine of those definitive ones, then followed it with relating the statement of these others. So it is necessary that these be different from the first group.

* * *

Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And there will appear to them﴾ — that is, in the Hereafter — ﴿the evils of what they did,﴾ while they had previously considered them good deeds. So this became the first of their loss. ﴿And there will befall them what they used to mock.﴾ This is like evidence that this group, when they said ﴿we only assume an assumption﴾, were speaking in the manner of mockery and derision. On this view, this group is worse than the first group, because the first were deniers and were not mockers, whereas this group added mockery to their persistence in denial.

* * *

Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And it will be said, "Today We forget you as you forgot the meeting of this your day."﴾ Concerning the interpretation of this forgetting there are two views:

The first: We leave you in punishment as you left obedience, which is the provision for the Day of Return.

The second: We make you like a forgotten thing, not cared for, just as you did not care about the meeting of this your day and did not turn toward it, but made it like a thing that is cast away as forgotten.

So God, exalted is He, gathered upon them three things from among the aspects of severe punishment:

The first of them: the complete cutting off of God's mercy from them.

The second: that their refuge becomes the Fire.

The third: that they will have no reward from helpers and supporters.

Then God, exalted is He, clarified that it will be said to them: you became deserving of these three aspects of severe punishment only because you committed three kinds of evil deeds:

The first of them: persistence in denying the true religion.

The second: mocking it and deriding it.

These two aspects are included under His saying, exalted is He: ﴿That is because you took the signs of God in mockery.﴾

The third: complete immersion in love of the world and total turning away from the Hereafter, and this is what is meant by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the worldly life deceived you.﴾

* * *

Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿So today they will not be brought out of it.﴾ Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read "yakhrujuna" with an open ya', and the rest read it with a damma. ﴿Nor will they be allowed to seek to please Him﴾ — that is, it will not be demanded of them that they please their Lord, that is, satisfy Him.

When the discussion of these noble, spiritual topics was complete, He concluded the surah with praising God, exalted is He, saying: ﴿So to God belongs praise, Lord of the heavens and Lord of the earth, Lord of the worlds.﴾ That is: praise God, who is the Creator of the heavens and the earth, indeed the Creator of all the worlds, of bodies, spirits, essences and attributes. For this lordship necessitates praise and commendation for every one of the created and nurtured beings.

* * *

Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And to Him belongs grandeur in the heavens and the earth.﴾ This indicates two matters:

One of them: that magnifying (takbir) must come after praising (tahmid), and it is an indication that when those who praise Him have praised Him, they must recognize that He is higher and greater than that the praise they have offered should be fitting for His bounty; rather He is greater than the praise of those who praise, and His favors are higher and more exalted than the gratitude of the grateful.

The second: that this grandeur belongs to Him and not to another, because the Necessarily Existent in Its essence is none other than He.

* * *

Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And He is the Mighty, the Wise.﴾ That is, by the perfection of His power He is able to create whatever He wills, and by the perfection of His wisdom He assigns to each kind of His creatures the effects of wisdom, mercy, bounty and generosity. His saying, ﴿and He is the Mighty, the Wise,﴾ conveys restriction (hasr). This indicates that none is perfect in power, wisdom and mercy except Him, and that indicates that there is no god for creation except Him, and no benefactor and no bestower of favor except Him.

Our master, may God be pleased with him, said: The interpretation of this surah was completed on Friday after the prayer, on the fifteenth of Dhu al-Hijjah in the year six hundred and three, and praise belongs to God, a good, blessed praise, perpetual and everlasting, as befits the loftiness of His station, the brilliance of His proof and the magnitude of His benevolence. And blessings upon the pure, sanctified spirits of those who dwell in the highest heavens and the depths of the earths, of the angels, the prophets, the saints and the monotheists, especially upon our master and our Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), and his family and all his companions.

The first of these is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And on the day the Hour is established, on that day the falsifiers will lose.﴾ Concerning this there are several discussions:

The first discussion: the governing element of the accusative in "the day the Hour is established" is "will lose," and "on that day" is a substitute for "the day the Hour is established."

The second discussion: We have mentioned in several places in this book that life, reason and health are, as it were, capital, and the disposal of them in seeking the happiness of the Hereafter proceeds in the manner of a merchant's disposal of his capital in seeking profit. The disbelievers have exhausted themselves in these dispositions, and they found from them nothing but deprivation and abandonment. Thus that, in reality, was the utmost of loss.

Second: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And you will see every nation kneeling.﴾ Al-Layth said: "al-juthuww" is sitting on the knees, as one kneels before a judge. Al-Zajjaj said: "Similar to it is jadha, yajdhu." The author of al-Kashshaf said: "It was also recited as jadhiyah." The lexicographers said: "al-judhuww" is more intense in its bracing than "al-juthuww," because the one who is jadhi is the one who sits on the tips of his toes. It is related from Ibn 'Abbas: "jathiyah" means gathered together, awaiting what will be done with them.

* * *

Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Every nation will be called to its record,﴾ with "every nation" in the nominative as the subject, and "every nation" as a substitute for "every nation" [the earlier one]. His saying "to its record" means to the pages of its deeds. He suffices with the generic noun, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the Book will be placed, and you will see the criminals fearful of what is in it﴾ [al-Kahf: 49]. The apparent meaning is that both believers and disbelievers are included, because of His saying after that: ﴿As for those who believed.﴾

* * *

Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿As for those who disbelieved.﴾ If it is said: kneeling on the knee befits only one who fears, and the believers have no fear on the Day of Resurrection. We say: the one who is righteous and secure may share with the falsifier in such a state until it becomes manifest that he is righteous.

It is "their book" in the sense that it is the book containing their deeds, and it is "God's Book" in the sense that He is the One who commanded the angels to write it. ﴿It speaks against you﴾ means it bears witness against you for what you did, without addition or subtraction. ﴿Indeed, We used to have copies made﴾ — the angels — ﴿of what you used to do﴾, that is, We used to have your deeds written down.

**Verses 27–37**

﴿To God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. And on the day the Hour is established, on that day the falsifiers will lose.﴾ ﴿And you will see every nation kneeling. Every nation will be called to its record: "Today you will be recompensed for what you used to do."﴾ ﴿This is Our record, speaking against you with truth. Indeed, We used to have copies made of what you used to do.﴾ ﴿As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, their Lord will admit them into His mercy. That is the clear triumph.﴾ ﴿As for those who disbelieved: "Were My verses not recited to you? But you were arrogant and were a criminal people."﴾

When it is established that God is capable of all possible things, and it is established that the occurrence of life in this essence is possible (for if it were not possible, it would not have occurred the first time), it follows from these two premises that He, exalted is He, is capable of bringing life a second time.

When God, exalted is He, clarified the possibility of speaking of the Gathering and the Resurrection by these two ways, He mentioned the details of the conditions of the Resurrection. The first of these is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And on the day the Hour is established, on that day the falsifiers will lose.﴾ Concerning this there are several discussions:

The first discussion: the governing element of the accusative in "the day the Hour is established" is "will lose," and "on that day" is a substitute for "the day the Hour is established."

The second discussion: We have mentioned in several places in this book that life, reason and health are, as it were, capital, and the disposal of them in seeking the happiness of the Hereafter proceeds in the manner of a merchant's disposal of his capital in seeking profit. The disbelievers have exhausted themselves in these dispositions, and they found from them nothing but deprivation and abandonment. Thus that, in reality, was the utmost of loss.

Second: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And you will see every nation kneeling.﴾ Al-Layth said: "al-juthuww" is sitting on the knees, as one kneels before a judge. Al-Zajjaj said: "Similar to it is jadha, yajdhu." The author of al-Kashshaf said: "It was also recited as jadhiyah." The lexicographers said: "al-judhuww" is more intense in its bracing than "al-juthuww," because the one who is jadhi is the one who sits on the tips of his toes. It is related from Ibn 'Abbas: "jathiyah" means gathered together, awaiting what will be done with them.

* * *

Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Every nation will be called to its record,﴾ with "every nation" in the nominative as the subject, and "every nation" as a substitute for "every nation" [the earlier one]. His saying "to its record" means to the pages of its deeds. He suffices with the generic noun, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the Book will be placed, and you will see the criminals fearful of what is in it﴾ [al-Kahf: 49]. The apparent meaning is that both believers and disbelievers are included, because of His saying after that: ﴿As for those who believed.﴾

* * *

Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿As for those who disbelieved.﴾ If it is said: kneeling on the knee befits only one who fears, and the believers have no fear on the Day of Resurrection. We say: the one who is righteous and secure may share with the falsifier in such a state until it becomes manifest that he is righteous.

* * *

Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Today you will be recompensed.﴾ The implied meaning is: it will be said to them, "Today you will be recompensed." If it is said: how is the Book attributed to them and to God, exalted is He? We say: there is no contradiction between the two matters. It is "their book" in the sense that it is the book containing their deeds, and it is "God's Book" in the sense that He is the One who commanded the angels to write it. ﴿It speaks against you﴾ means it bears witness against you for what you did, without addition or subtraction. ﴿Indeed, We used to have copies made﴾ — the angels — ﴿of what you used to do﴾, that is, We used to have your deeds written down.

Then He clarified the condition of the obedient, saying: ﴿As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, their Lord will admit them into His mercy. That is the clear triumph.﴾ Concerning this there are several issues:

The first issue: after describing them with faith, He mentioned that they were doing righteous deeds, so it is necessary that doing righteous deeds be different from faith and additional to it.

The second issue: the Mu'tazilites (a theological school) said: He made entry into God's mercy conditional upon their bringing faith and righteous deeds together, and what is conditional upon two matters together is nonexistent when one of them is absent. So when righteous deeds are absent, it is necessary that the triumph of Paradise not be attained. Our answer: making a ruling conditional upon an attribute does not indicate the absence of the ruling when the attribute is absent.

The third issue: He called the reward "mercy," and mercy can properly be called by this name only when it is not obligatory. Therefore it is necessary that reward not be obligatory upon God, exalted is He.

* * *

Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿As for those who disbelieved: "Were My verses not recited to you? But you were arrogant and were a criminal people."﴾ Concerning this there are several issues:

The first issue: God mentioned the believers and the disbelievers and did not mention a third category. This indicates that the doctrine of the Mu'tazilites, that of an intermediate position (between belief and disbelief), is false.

The second issue: He gave as the reason for the deserving of punishment that His verses were recited to them and they were arrogant toward accepting them. This indicates that the deserving of punishment does not occur except after the coming of the Law (shar'), and that indicates that obligations are not obligatory except through the Law, contrary to what the Mu'tazilites say, that some obligations may be obligatory by reason ('aql).

The third issue: the answer to "as for" (amma) is omitted, and the implied meaning is: "As for those who disbelieved, it will be said to them: 'Were My verses not recited to you? But you were arrogant'" toward accepting the truth, "and you were a criminal people"? If they say: how is it good to describe the disbeliever as a criminal, in the context of censure and blame directed at him? We say: its meaning is that they, despite being disbelievers, were not upright in their own religions; rather they were corrupt in that religion. And God knows best.

* * *

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when it was said, "Indeed, the promise of God is true, and the Hour, there is no doubt in it," you said, "We do not know what the Hour is; we only assume an assumption, and we are not certain."﴾ ﴿And there will appear to them the evils of what they did, and there will befall them what they used to mock.﴾ ﴿And it will be said, "Today We forget you as you forgot the meeting of this your day. Your refuge is the Fire, and you have no helpers."﴾ ﴿That is because you took the signs of God in mockery, and the worldly life deceived you. So today they will not be brought out of it, nor will they be allowed to seek to please Him.﴾ ﴿So to God belongs praise, Lord of the heavens and Lord of the earth, Lord of the worlds.﴾ ﴿And to Him belongs grandeur in the heavens and the earth, and He is the Mighty, the Wise.﴾ Concerning this there are several issues:

The first issue: "and the Hour" was recited in both the nominative and the accusative. Al-Zajjaj said: whoever reads it in the accusative makes it conjoined to "the promise," and whoever reads it in the nominative does so in the sense of "and it was said: 'the Hour, there is no doubt in it.'" Al-Akhfash said: the nominative is better in meaning and more common in Arabic speech when it comes after the predicate of "inna," because it is a sentence standing on its own after the first sentence has been completed in full.

The second issue: God, exalted is He, related about the disbelievers that when it was said to them that God's promise of reward and punishment is true, and that the Hour is coming, there is no doubt in it, they said: "We do not know what the Hour is; we only assume an assumption, and we are not certain."

I say: the more probable view is that the people were, on this matter, of two positions. Among them were those who were definitively denying resurrection and the Hour, and they are those whom God mentioned in the preceding verse by His saying: ﴿And they said: there is nothing but our worldly life.﴾ And among them were those who were doubtful and bewildered about it, because from the great amount they had heard from the Messenger (ﷺ), and from the great amount of evidence they had heard in support of its truth, they became doubtful about it. These are the ones whom this verse intends. What indicates this is that He, exalted is He, related the doctrine of those definitive ones, then followed it with relating the statement of these others. So it is necessary that these be different from the first group.

* * *

Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And there will appear to them﴾ — that is, in the Hereafter — ﴿the evils of what they did,﴾ while they had previously considered them good deeds. So this became the first of their loss. ﴿And there will befall them what they used to mock.﴾ This is like evidence that this group, when they said ﴿we only assume an assumption﴾, were speaking in the manner of mockery and derision. On this view, this group is worse than the first group, because the first were deniers and were not mockers, whereas this group added mockery to their persistence in denial.

* * *

Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And it will be said, "Today We forget you as you forgot the meeting of this your day."﴾ Concerning the interpretation of this forgetting there are two views:

The first: We leave you in punishment as you left obedience, which is the provision for the Day of Return.

The second: We make you like a forgotten thing, not cared for, just as you did not care about the meeting of this your day and did not turn toward it, but made it like a thing that is cast away as forgotten.

So God, exalted is He, gathered upon them three things from among the aspects of severe punishment:

The first of them: the complete cutting off of God's mercy from them.

The second: that their refuge becomes the Fire.

The third: that they will have no reward from helpers and supporters.

Then God, exalted is He, clarified that it will be said to them: you became deserving of these three aspects of severe punishment only because you committed three kinds of evil deeds:

The first of them: persistence in denying the true religion.

The second: mocking it and deriding it.

These two aspects are included under His saying, exalted is He: ﴿That is because you took the signs of God in mockery.﴾

The third: complete immersion in love of the world and total turning away from the Hereafter, and this is what is meant by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the worldly life deceived you.﴾

* * *

Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿So today they will not be brought out of it.﴾ Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read "yakhrujuna" with an open ya', and the rest read it with a damma. ﴿Nor will they be allowed to seek to please Him﴾ — that is, it will not be demanded of them that they please their Lord, that is, satisfy Him.

When the discussion of these noble, spiritual topics was complete, He concluded the surah with praising God, exalted is He, saying: ﴿So to God belongs praise, Lord of the heavens and Lord of the earth, Lord of the worlds.﴾ That is: praise God, who is the Creator of the heavens and the earth, indeed the Creator of all the worlds, of bodies, spirits, essences and attributes. For this lordship necessitates praise and commendation for every one of the created and nurtured beings.

* * *

Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And to Him belongs grandeur in the heavens and the earth.﴾ This indicates two matters:

One of them: that magnifying (takbir) must come after praising (tahmid), and it is an indication that when those who praise Him have praised Him, they must recognize that He is higher and greater than that the praise they have offered should be fitting for His bounty; rather He is greater than the praise of those who praise, and His favors are higher and more exalted than the gratitude of the grateful.

The second: that this grandeur belongs to Him and not to another, because the Necessarily Existent in Its essence is none other than He.

* * *

* * *

* * *

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when it was said, "Indeed, the promise of God is true, and the Hour, there is no doubt in it," you said, "We do not know what the Hour is; we only assume an assumption, and we are not certain."﴾ ﴿And there will appear to them the evils of what they did, and there will befall them what they used to mock.﴾ ﴿And it will be said, "Today We forget you as you forgot the meeting of this your day. Your refuge is the Fire, and you have no helpers."﴾ ﴿That is because you took the signs of God in mockery, and the worldly life deceived you. So today they will not be brought out of it, nor will they be allowed to seek to please Him.﴾ ﴿So to God belongs praise, Lord of the heavens and Lord of the earth, Lord of the worlds.﴾ ﴿And to Him belongs grandeur in the heavens and the earth, and He is the Mighty, the Wise.﴾ Concerning this there are several issues:

The first issue: "and the Hour" was recited in both the nominative and the accusative. Al-Zajjaj said: whoever reads it in the accusative makes it conjoined to "the promise," and whoever reads it in the nominative does so in the sense of "and it was said: 'the Hour, there is no doubt in it.'" I say: the more probable view is that the people were, on this matter, of two positions. Among them were those who were definitively denying resurrection and the Hour, and they are those whom God mentioned in the preceding verse by His saying: ﴿And they said: there is nothing but our worldly life.﴾ And among them were those who were doubtful and bewildered about it, because from the great amount they had heard from the Messenger (ﷺ), and from the great amount of evidence they had heard in support of its truth, they became doubtful about it. These are the ones whom this verse intends. What indicates this is that He, exalted is He, related the doctrine of those definitive ones, then followed it with relating the statement of these others. So it is necessary that these be different from the first group.

* * *

Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And there will appear to them﴾ — that is, in the Hereafter — ﴿the evils of what they did,﴾ while they had previously considered them good deeds. So this became the first of their loss. ﴿And there will befall them what they used to mock.﴾ This is like evidence that this group, when they said ﴿we only assume an assumption﴾, were speaking in the manner of mockery and derision. On this view, this group is worse than the first group, because the first were deniers and were not mockers, whereas this group added mockery to their persistence in denial.

* * *

Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And it will be said, "Today We forget you as you forgot the meeting of this your day."﴾ Concerning the interpretation of this forgetting there are two views:

The first: We leave you in punishment as you left obedience, which is the provision for the Day of Return.

The second: We make you like a forgotten thing, not cared for, just as you did not care about the meeting of this your day and did not turn toward it, but made it like a thing that is cast away as forgotten.

So God, exalted is He, gathered upon them three things from among the aspects of severe punishment:

The first of them: the complete cutting off of God's mercy from them.

The second: that their refuge becomes the Fire.

The third: that they will have no reward from helpers and supporters.

Then God, exalted is He, clarified that it will be said to them: you became deserving of these three aspects of severe punishment only because you committed three kinds of evil deeds:

The first of them: persistence in denying the true religion.

The second: mocking it and deriding it.

These two aspects are included under His saying, exalted is He: ﴿That is because you took the signs of God in mockery.﴾

The third: complete immersion in love of the world and total turning away from the Hereafter, and this is what is meant by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the worldly life deceived you.﴾

* * *

Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿So today they will not be brought out of it.﴾ Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read "yakhrujuna" with an open ya', and the rest read it with a damma. ﴿Nor will they be allowed to seek to please Him﴾ — that is, it will not be demanded of them that they please their Lord, that is, satisfy Him.

When the discussion of these noble, spiritual topics was complete, He concluded the surah with praising God, exalted is He, saying: ﴿So to God belongs praise, Lord of the heavens and Lord of the earth, Lord of the worlds.﴾ That is: praise God, who is the Creator of the heavens and the earth, indeed the Creator of all the worlds, of bodies, spirits, essences and attributes. For this lordship necessitates praise and commendation for every one of the created and nurtured beings.

* * *

Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And to Him belongs grandeur in the heavens and the earth.﴾ This indicates two matters:

One of them: that magnifying (takbir) must come after praising (tahmid), and it is an indication that when those who praise Him have praised Him, they must recognize that He is higher and greater than that the praise they have offered should be fitting for His bounty; rather He is greater than the praise of those who praise, and His favors are higher and more exalted than the gratitude of the grateful.

The second: that this grandeur belongs to Him and not to another, because the Necessarily Existent in Its essence is none other than He.

* * *

Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And He is the Mighty, the Wise.﴾ That is, by the perfection of His power He is able to create whatever He wills, and by the perfection of His wisdom He assigns to each kind of His creatures the effects of wisdom, mercy, bounty and generosity. His saying, ﴿and He is the Mighty, the Wise,﴾ conveys restriction (hasr). This indicates that none is perfect in power, wisdom and mercy except Him, and that indicates that there is no god for creation except Him, and no benefactor and no bestower of favor except Him.

Our master, may God be pleased with him, said: The interpretation of this surah was completed on Friday after the prayer, on the fifteenth of Dhu al-Hijjah in the year six hundred and three, and praise belongs to God, a good, blessed praise, perpetual and everlasting, as befits the loftiness of His station, the brilliance of His proof and the magnitude of His benevolence. And blessings upon the pure, sanctified spirits of those who dwell in the highest heavens and the depths of the earths, of the angels, the prophets, the saints and the monotheists, especially upon our master and our Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), and his family and all his companions.

* * *

Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And there will appear to them﴾ — that is, in the Hereafter — ﴿the evils of what they did,﴾ while they had previously considered them good deeds. * * *

Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And it will be said, "Today We forget you as you forgot the meeting of this your day."﴾ Concerning the interpretation of this forgetting there are two views:

The second: that their refuge becomes the Fire.

The third: that they will have no reward from helpers and supporters.

* * *

* * *

Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And to Him belongs grandeur in the heavens and the earth.﴾ This indicates two matters:

* * *

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when it was said, "Indeed, the promise of God is true, and the Hour, there is no doubt in it," you said, "We do not know what the Hour is; we only assume an assumption, and we are not certain."﴾ ﴿And there will appear to them the evils of what they did, and there will befall them what they used to mock.﴾ ﴿And it will be said, "Today We forget you as you forgot the meeting of this your day. Your refuge is the Fire, and you have no helpers."﴾ ﴿That is because you took the signs of God in mockery, and the worldly life deceived you. So today they will not be brought out of it, nor will they be allowed to seek to please Him.﴾ ﴿So to God belongs praise, Lord of the heavens and Lord of the earth, Lord of the worlds.﴾ ﴿And to Him belongs grandeur in the heavens and the earth, and He is the Mighty, the Wise.﴾ Concerning this there are several issues:

The first issue: "and the Hour" was recited in both the nominative and the accusative. Al-Zajjaj said: whoever reads it in the accusative makes it conjoined to "the promise," and whoever reads it in the nominative does so in the sense of "and it was said: 'the Hour, there is no doubt in it.'" Al-Akhfash said: the nominative is better in meaning and more common in Arabic speech when it comes after the predicate of "inna," because it is a sentence standing on its own after the first sentence has been completed in full.

The second issue: God, exalted is He, related about the disbelievers that when it was said to them that God's promise of reward and punishment is true, and that the Hour is coming, there is no doubt in it, they said: "We do not know what the Hour is; we only assume an assumption, and we are not certain."

I say: the more probable view is that the people were, on this matter, of two positions. Among them were those who were definitively denying resurrection and the Hour, and they are those whom God mentioned in the preceding verse by His saying: ﴿And they said: there is nothing but our worldly life.﴾ And among them were those who were doubtful and bewildered about it, because from the great amount they had heard from the Messenger (ﷺ), and from the great amount of evidence they had heard in support of its truth, they became doubtful about it. These are the ones whom this verse intends. What indicates this is that He, exalted is He, related the doctrine of those definitive ones, then followed it with relating the statement of these others. So it is necessary that these be different from the first group.

* * *

Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And there will appear to them﴾ — that is, in the Hereafter — ﴿the evils of what they did,﴾ while they had previously considered them good deeds. So this became the first of their loss. ﴿And there will befall them what they used to mock.﴾ This is like evidence that this group, when they said ﴿we only assume an assumption﴾, were speaking in the manner of mockery and derision. On this view, this group is worse than the first group, because the first were deniers and were not mockers, whereas this group added mockery to their persistence in denial.

* * *

Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And it will be said, "Today We forget you as you forgot the meeting of this your day."﴾ Concerning the interpretation of this forgetting there are two views:

The first: We leave you in punishment as you left obedience, which is the provision for the Day of Return.

The second: We make you like a forgotten thing, not cared for, just as you did not care about the meeting of this your day and did not turn toward it, but made it like a thing that is cast away as forgotten.

So God, exalted is He, gathered upon them three things from among the aspects of severe punishment:

The first of them: the complete cutting off of God's mercy from them.

The second: that their refuge becomes the Fire.

The third: that they will have no reward from helpers and supporters.

Then God, exalted is He, clarified that it will be said to them: you became deserving of these three aspects of severe punishment only because you committed three kinds of evil deeds:

The first of them: persistence in denying the true religion.

The second: mocking it and deriding it.

These two aspects are included under His saying, exalted is He: ﴿That is because you took the signs of God in mockery.﴾

The third: complete immersion in love of the world and total turning away from the Hereafter, and this is what is meant by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the worldly life deceived you.﴾

* * *

Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿So today they will not be brought out of it.﴾ Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read "yakhrujuna" with an open ya', and the rest read it with a damma. ﴿Nor will they be allowed to seek to please Him﴾ — that is, it will not be demanded of them that they please their Lord, that is, satisfy Him.

When the discussion of these noble, spiritual topics was complete, He concluded the surah with praising God, exalted is He, saying: ﴿So to God belongs praise, Lord of the heavens and Lord of the earth, Lord of the worlds.﴾ That is: praise God, who is the Creator of the heavens and the earth, indeed the Creator of all the worlds, of bodies, spirits, essences and attributes. For this lordship necessitates praise and commendation for every one of the created and nurtured beings.

* * *

Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And to Him belongs grandeur in the heavens and the earth.﴾ This indicates two matters:

One of them: that magnifying (takbir) must come after praising (tahmid), and it is an indication that when those who praise Him have praised Him, they must recognize that He is higher and greater than that the praise they have offered should be fitting for His bounty; rather He is greater than the praise of those who praise, and His favors are higher and more exalted than the gratitude of the grateful.

The second: that this grandeur belongs to Him and not to another, because the Necessarily Existent in Its essence is none other than He.

* * *

Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And He is the Mighty, the Wise.﴾ That is, by the perfection of His power He is able to create whatever He wills, and by the perfection of His wisdom He assigns to each kind of His creatures the effects of wisdom, mercy, bounty and generosity. His saying, ﴿and He is the Mighty, the Wise,﴾ conveys restriction (hasr). This indicates that none is perfect in power, wisdom and mercy except Him, and that indicates that there is no god for creation except Him, and no benefactor and no bestower of favor except Him.

Our master, may God be pleased with him, said: The interpretation of this surah was completed on Friday after the prayer, on the fifteenth of Dhu al-Hijjah in the year six hundred and three, and praise belongs to God, a good, blessed praise, perpetual and everlasting, as befits the loftiness of His station, the brilliance of His proof and the magnitude of His benevolence. And blessings upon the pure, sanctified spirits of those who dwell in the highest heavens and the depths of the earths, of the angels, the prophets, the saints and the monotheists, especially upon our master and our Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), and his family and all his companions.
